data.title: Malware found in official gravityforms plugin indicating supply chain breach
data.author: taubek
data.article_summary: 文章报道了GravityForms插件官方版本中发现恶意软件，表明存在供应链 breach。最初在7月10日发现问题，恶意代码通过HTTP请求连接到可疑的gravityapi.org域名。技术分析显示，恶意代码收集网站信息并发送至该域名。GravityForms在版本2.9.12中包含后门，但随后迅速移除。7月11日，发布2.9.13版本修复问题，Namecheap也暂停了相关域名。监控显示感染范围不大，仅影响手动下载和composer安装。Patchstack团队正在调查，并提醒用户检查是否受影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Gravity Forms安全事件的细节、影响范围及可能原因

不同观点：
• neomantra认为，此次安全 breach 能够被发现，得益于系统操作员的 diligent tracking，类似于之前xz breach通过开发者发现异常性能回归而被揭露。这表明细致的监控对发现安全问题至关重要。
• anthonyeden引用了Gravity Forms的官方声明，指出只有通过直接下载或Composer安装的用户会受到影响，并关注到官方尚未提及是否会聘请第三方安全公司调查此事。
• rectang转述了RocketGenius工作人员的确认，即恶意软件只影响手动下载和通过Composer安装的插件，对此表示松了一口气。
• mpol指出，如果在检查表单之前使用nonce，可以防止许多问题，暗示这能减少手动工作量，强调技术措施在防范中的作用。
• doodlebugging对文章中的日期错误表示关注，认为这是编辑上的失误，虽然不影响事件本身，但可能影响读者理解。
• hammyhavoc质疑此次安全问题未被及时发现的时间长度，表明对响应速度的担忧。
• bhk关注此次事件的影响范围，询问是广泛影响互联网上的大量网站，还是仅限于少数低流量网站。
• mmsc仅简短提及了Ac1dB1tch3z，没有深入讨论。
• giingyui认为应明确指出涉及的插件名称，以增加透明度。
• kristianc批评了Gravity Forms的高价扩展，质疑这是否反映了WordPress生态系统的问题，包括其安全性、开发者可能的欺诈行为以及非技术用户的易受骗性。
• iambateman对事件的可能性质提出疑问，怀疑是否是GravityForms内部人员所为，并指出文章中未明确说明此事。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是事件的发现和透明度，部分评论（如neomantra和anthonyeden）关注发现过程及官方回应的充分性。
• 另一个讨论点是事件的技术细节，如mpol对nonce使用的建议，表明如何通过技术手段防止类似问题。
• 事件的影响范围和可能的原因也是讨论的重点，bhk和iambateman对此提出了具体的疑问和猜测。
• 最后，kristianc对WordPress生态系统的广泛批评引发对高价插件和用户安全的思考。

Rafie Muhammad
Lead Security Researcher at Patchstack
Supply Chain Attack
Security Advisories

Update 8-11-2025 06:00 UTC:
We have observed some activity in regard to one of the backdoors that involves a gf_api_token parameter. The IP address 193.160.101.6 tries to request, for every site, the following URLs with a spoofed user agent:
/wp-content/plugins/gravityforms_2.9.12/notification.php?gf_api_token=Cx3VGSwAHkB9yzIL9Qi48IFHwKm4sQ6Te5odNtBYu6Asb9JX06KYAWmrfPtG1eP3&action=ping
/wp-content/plugins/gravityforms_2.9.11.1/notification.php?gf_api_token=Cx3VGSwAHkB9yzIL9Qi48IFHwKm4sQ6Te5odNtBYu6Asb9JX06KYAWmrfPtG1eP3&action=ping
/wp-content/plugins/gravityforms/notification.php?gf_api_token=Cx3VGSwAHkB9yzIL9Qi48IFHwKm4sQ6Te5odNtBYu6Asb9JX06KYAWmrfPtG1eP3&action=ping
Update 7-11-2025 14:10 UTC
: A version
2.9.13
has been released to ensure customers can safely update to a new version without a backdoor present. In addition, Namecheap (the domain registrar) has suspended the domain name gravityapi.org to avoid successful exploitation of the backdoor portion that connects to this domain name.
Update 7-11-2025 12:38 UTC
: We received from our reporter both the copy of the vulnerable version and the patched version of the plugin. Technical details are updated in this article. We also received a confirmation from one of the staff of RocketGenius that the malware only affects manual downloads and composer installation of the plugin.
Update 7-11-2025 12:07 UTC
: We received information from our reporter that GravityForm responded to his initial email and confirmed that they are doing an investigation for a malware breach on their product. The reporter claims that the initial malicious code was found in version
2.9.12
(which is the latest version of the plugin currently); however, the malicious code itself has now been removed from the code when users try to re-download the package. We also updated more IOCs in this article.
Update 7-11-2025 12:00 UTC
: We've been in touch with multiple large web hosting companies who have scanned their servers for the IOCs. The infection does not seem to be widespread, which could mean that the backdoored plugin was only available for a very short period of time and only delivered to a small number of users.
The
Patchstack team
has been monitoring targeted supply chain attacks involving a vendor of a plugin or theme. At first, we noticed that Groundhogg was affected by this supply chain attack, and its plugins were compromised by malware that was injected. The full details can be viewed
here
.
Today, we received information about a possible targeted supply chain attack against
Gravity Forms
. We are still actively investigating to better understand the scale and impact, but as we have proof of infected websites and IOCs to keep an eye on, we're sharing this information in this post so people could check if they have been affected.

gravityforms.com
domain contains a suspicious HTTP request to the
gravityapi.org
domain. This suspicious HTTP request call was flagged by the reporter because they noticed that there is an extremely slow request to that domain per their monitoring system.

gravityforms/common.php

data.title: Chrome's hidden X-Browser-Validation header reverse engineered
data.author: dsekz
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一个针对Chrome浏览器私有头部"x-browser-validation"的反向工程与生成工具。该头部用于完整性验证，确保用户代理与平台匹配，防止伪造。该头部通过连接平台特定的API密钥和用户代理字符串，使用SHA-1算法进行哈希，然后进行Base64编码生成。文章提供了生成该头部的Python代码示例，并详细描述了反向工程过程，包括在Chrome二进制文件中找到相关函数和算法。最终确认该头部的生成过程为：API密钥 + 用户代理字符串 → SHA-1哈希 → Base64编码。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Chrome浏览器中的"x-browser-validation"头部生成机制及其潜在目的和影响

不同观点：
• [dsekz] 提出对"x-browser-validation"头部的技术分析，并提供代码证明，主要关注该头部的生成方式及其潜在用途（如反欺诈、完整性验证等）。
• [userbinator] 担心该头部是Google通过法律手段打压竞争的一部分，类似于历史上Sega v. Accolade案件，并质疑为何使用SHA-1而不是其他哈希算法。
• [cebert] 认为该头部是Google用来区分用户请求和机器请求的手段，同时担心其会进一步用于用户指纹识别。
• [dlenski] 关注该头部是否在开源的Chromium中也存在，还是仅限于闭源的Chrome。
• [jakub_g] 猜测该头部与Google企业版功能（如限制登录仅支持Chrome浏览器）有关。
• [thayne] 提到Google刚输掉反垄断诉讼，质疑此时推出该头部的动机，并担心该头部可能被用于反竞争行为，同时提到该头部被逆向工程后可能被伪造。
• [binary132] 认为Google有权构建自己的私有网络，但担心其试图将整个互联网变成私有，表达了对这种趋势的不满。
• [egorfine] 询问是否有方法阻止Chrome发送这些头部。
• [aussieguy1234] 认为该头部是一种隐藏的客户端验证机制。
• [RandyOrion] 提出两个具体问题：该头部从哪个Chrome版本开始实现，以及其对Chromium非谷歌版本的影响。
• [_imnothere] 强烈反对这种验证机制的存在，认为只有Google内部人员会支持这种做法。
• [Everdred2dx] 担心该头部可能泄露用户的真实用户代理（UA）。
• [Larrikin] 询问如何在Firefox中设置类似的头部。
• [delusional] 质疑该头部是否受版权保护，并讨论伪造这种头部是否构成版权侵权，认为这种可能性很奇怪。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Google引入该头部的真实目的及其潜在的反竞争影响。
• 技术细节如哈希算法的选择（SHA-1）也引发了讨论。
• 用户隐私问题，尤其是指纹识别和用户代理泄露，也是关注重点。
• 开源与闭源的区别，以及该头部对不同浏览器版本的影响被提及。
• 如何阻止或伪造这些头部是另一个值得注意的讨论点。

Chrome X-Browser-Validation Header Reverse Engineering & Generator
Chrome recently added a few new headers:
"x-browser-channel": "stable",
"x-browser-copyright": "Copyright 2025 Google LLC. All rights reserved.",
"x-browser-validation": "6h3XF8YcD8syi2FF2BbuE2KllQo=",
"x-browser-year": "2025"
Apart from one of them, there isn’t much that’s interesting. They’re just bits of client specific information. However, base64 decoding x-browser-validation yields what appears to be a hash whose purpose remains undocumented.
Chrome almost certainly uses this header as an integrity signal. Verifying that the declared user agent matches the underlying platform, spotting user agent string spoofing attempts etc.
Generator
from
xbv
import
generate_validation_header
ua
=
"Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/138.0.0.0 Safari/537.36"
# You may supply an explicit api_key alongside the ua
# if omitted, the function automatically selects the appropriate key based on the user agent
api_key
=
"AIzaSyA2KlwBX3mkFo30om9LUFYQhpqLoa_BNhE"
header_value
=
generate_validation_header
(
ua
)
print
(
header_value
)
How the Header Is Made
Grab two strings
A hard-coded, platform specific API key
The browser’s full user agent string
Concatenate
DATA = API_KEY + USER_AGENT
Hash
DATA
with SHA-1 and base64 encode it.
Platform API Keys
Platform
Default Key (found in Chrome binaries)
Windows
AIzaSyA2KlwBX3mkFo30om9LUFYQhpqLoa_BNhE
Linux
AIzaSyBqJZh-7pA44blAaAkH6490hUFOwX0KCYM
macOS
AIzaSyDr2UxVnv_U85AbhhY8XSHSIavUW0DC-sY
Reverse-Engineering
Opened
chrome.dll
in IDA. The master routine
sub_1806C95B0
builds every
X-Browser-*
header (you can find this function by searching
browser-validation
etc):
Data prep - grabs the first hard-coded API key for the OS and appends the full user agent.
__int64
__fastcall
sub_1806C95B0
(
__int64
a1
,
__int64
a2
)
{
// ... setup ...
// Data Preparation
// Retrieves credentials and combines the API key and user agent into a buffer.
v7
=
sub_1806C9B30
();
v9
=
sub_183EBC7D0
(
v41
,
0LL
,
v7
,
v8
);
// ... more setup ...
// Hashing
// The call to the SHA-1 hashing function.
sub_183B509D0
(
v46
,
v38
);
// ... more setup ...
// Encoding
// The call to the Base64 encoding function.
sub_1806C9A80
((
__int64
*
)
v40
,
v39
);
// ... more setup ...
// Header Setting
// Adds the final encoded string to the request headers.
v30
=
"X-Browser-Validation"
;
sub_183C6B920
(
v27
);
// ...
}
Hash - passes that buffer into
sub_183B509D0
, which is SHA-1 algo. Open this guy and the first assignment jumps out:
v12
[
0
]
=
xmmword_7FFE2C9A7D50
;
LODWORD
(
v12
[
1
])
=
-1009589776
;
// 0xC3D2E1F0
The second you see that "-1009589776" number, you can literally smell SHA-1.
Base64 - the 20-byte digest is encoded.
Dynamic confirmation: pause one instruction before the hash call, dump RDX, and the ~150-byte buffer is nothing but
<API_KEY><User-Agent>
Base64(SHA-1(buffer)) = header. Mystery solved.

• 技术细节如哈希算法的选择（SHA-1）也引发了讨论。
• 用户隐私问题，尤其是指纹识别和用户代理泄露，也是关注重点。
• 开源与闭源的区别，以及该头部对不同浏览器版本的影响被提及。

data.title: Hacking Coroutines into C
data.author: jmillikin
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了在一个嵌入式软件项目中，如何通过将协程概念引入C语言来简化状态机的实现。传统的状态机方法在处理多个状态和事件时，代码难以维护和理解。作者受高级语言中协程的启发，提出了一种在不使用操作系统的情况下实现类似协程的并发处理方法。文章通过一个LED闪烁控制和按钮按下时间记录的例子，展示了如何用状态机和轮询机制实现功能。虽然这种方法可行，但代码复杂且不易读。作者建议引入类似协程的机制，以简化逻辑流和状态管理，从而提高代码的可读性和可维护性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在C语言中实现轻量级协程和状态机的不同方法及其优缺点

不同观点：
• **adinisom** 支持使用基于结构体的轻量级Protothreads实现，通过`YIELD()`宏和手动状态管理，实现协程功能。他认为这种方法可以很好地结合声明式和过程式代码，并且在处理硬件相关代码时非常有效。
• **astrobe_** 认为状态机的控制流本质上是非线性的，使用goto语句可能会更清晰。他指出，状态机的可视化和模块化是一个问题，并建议使用图形化的DSL工具来解决。
• **mikepurvis** 提到FreeRTOS也可以使用协作式调度器，并倾向于使用真正的代码生成而不是宏来实现协程，以提高代码的可读性和调试能力。
• **userbinator** 认为使用PWM外设或定时器中断可以让CPU大部分时间处于 halt 状态，从而简化问题，比手动实现状态机更简单。
• **syncurrent** 提到同步语言如Esterel或Blech的类似方法，并提供了一个GitHub链接作为参考。
• **jonhohle** 分享了他使用libaco处理事件和流解压的经验，认为这种方法可以让代码保持线性结构。
• **Neywiny** 表示不喜欢在软件中使用状态机，认为状态机更适合硬件实现。他主张函数应根据需要写得尽量长，避免不必要的函数调用。
• **user____name** 对使用宏来模拟协程的复杂性表示质疑，认为语言级别的支持会更好，并提供了一篇关于fibers的文章作为参考。
• **codr7** 认为所展示的实现过于复杂，并提供了一个自己书中的替代方案链接。
• **moconnor** 提到其同事通过手动更新堆栈和jmp指令实现了协程，这种方法在超级计算中心使用多年。
• **webdevver** 提到有一个关于该主题的文章。
• **throwaway81523** 认为这种方法类似于多年前出现的protothreads，并对文章的CSS排版提出了批评。
• **Asooka** 建议使用CPC或改编qemu的协程，认为C语言中协程的实现有多种成熟方案。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于状态机和协程的实现复杂性、可读性和模块化问题。
• 不同的实现方法包括宏定义、手动状态管理、使用现有库（如FreeRTOS、libaco）、手动堆栈操作等。
• 可视化和调试是状态机实现中的一个重要问题，有人建议使用图形化工具来帮助解决。
• 有人提到语言级别的支持可能会更好地解决协程实现中的问题。

data.title: C++: Maps on Chains
data.author: signa11
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了在C++中使用`std::map`存储不重叠的整数区间时遇到的问题。默认情况下，`std::map`要求键具有严格的弱序关系，但区间之间可能存在不可比较的情况（如重叠），这违反了严格弱序的要求。文章分析了区间顺序为何不是严格弱序，并提出了一种解决方案：通过在比较操作符中检测和抛出重叠异常来避免未定义行为。这种方法通过确保每次插入的区间形成一个链来绕过问题，使得`std::map`可以在实际应用中正常工作。文章还提到通过异质查找（heterogeneous lookup）可以扩展功能，支持查找位于区间内的整数。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何存储和处理不重叠区间，特别是在C++中使用std::map或类似的数据结构时，如何设计比较运算符以及处理区间重叠的问题。

不同观点：
• [delifue] 认为应该通过最小端点来存储区间，并使用有序查询。这种方法强调了使用map结构来管理不重叠区间的基本思路，但未详细讨论区间重叠时的处理方式。
  
• [Gupie] 提出了具体的比较运算符实现，建议通过先比较最小端点，如果相等再比较最大端点的方式来实现排序。这种方法试图解决区间排序中的相等判断问题，但没有涉及区间重叠的处理。

• [diath] 对Gupie的比较运算符提出警告，指出这种实现可能会导致类似std::sort的崩溃问题。他引用了cppreference中的Compare概念要求，强调需要满足特定的比较运算符规范，以避免潜在的错误。

• [z_open] 认为抛出运行时错误并不是理想的解决方案，建议通过修改比较运算符或使用unordered_map来避免区间重叠问题。他提出了使用"x.min < y.min || (x.min == y.min && x.max < y.max)"的方式来定义比较运算符。

• [gsliepen] 对文章内容表示不满，认为文章没有深入探讨如何实现真正的区间映射（interval map）。他指出文章只是简单地提出在插入重叠区间时抛出异常，而不是展示如何处理这些区间，这并不具有建设性。

• [derriz] 完全反对文章中的做法，认为如果需求是防止添加重叠区间的元素，那么修改比较运算符并依赖std::map的排序机制是一种脆弱且不合理的解决方案。他指出，向map中添加键值对不应因为特定关系而抛出错误，这种设计是不合理的。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于如何正确地设计数据结构来存储不重叠区间。部分讨论者（如delifue和Gupie）关注比较运算符的具体实现，而另一些讨论者（如diath和derriz）则强调了潜在的错误和设计缺陷。
  
• 另一个值得注意的点是如何处理区间重叠。一些讨论者（如z_open和gsliepen）认为抛出异常并不是理想的解决方案，并提出了修改比较运算符或设计新的数据结构来解决这个问题。

• 讨论还涉及到对std::map适用性的质疑。derriz特别指出std::map并不适合处理这种需要防止区间重叠的需求，提出应该设计专门的区间数据结构。

44529274.article_content:
(From a conversation with Vassil Vassilev.) Suppose we want to have a C++ map where the keys are disjoint, integer intervals of the form [
a
,
b
]:
struct interval
{
int min, max;
};
std::map<interval, std::string> m;
m[{0, 9}] = "ABC";
m[{10, 19}] = "DEF";
This looks easy enough, we just have to write the proper comparison operator for intervals, right?
bool operator<(const interval& x, const interval& y)
{
return x.max < y.min;
}
But what happens if we try to insert an interval which is not disjoint with those already in the map?
m[{5, 14}] = "GHI"; // intersects both {0, 9} and {10, 19}
The short answer is that this is undefined behavior, but let's try to undertand why. C++ associative containers depend on the comparison function (typically,
std::less<Key>
) inducing a so-called
strict weak ordering
on elements of
Key
. In layman terms, a strict weak order < behaves as the "less than" relationship does for numbers, except that there may be incomparable elements
x
,
y
such that
x
≮
y
and
y
≮
x
; for numbers, this only happens if
x
=
y
, but in the case of a general SWO we allow for distinct, incomparable elements as long as they form
equivalence classes
. A convenient way to rephrase this condition is to require that incomparable elements are totally equivalent in how they compare to the rest of the elements, that is, they're truly indistinguishable from the point of view of the SWO. Getting back to our interval scenario, we have three possible cases when comparing [
a
,
b
] and [
c
,
d
]:
If
b
<
c
, the intervals don't overlap and [
a
,
b
] < [
c
,
d
].
If
d
<
a
, the intervals don't overlap and [
c
,
d
] < [
a
,
b
].
Otherwise, the intervals are incomparable. This can happen when [
a
,
b
] and [
c
,
d
] overlap partially or when they are exactly the same interval.
What we have described is a well known relationship called
interval order
. The problem is that the interval order is
not
a strict weak order. Let's depict a
Hasse diagram
for the interval order on integer intervals [
a
,
b
] between 0 and 4:
A Hasse diagram works like this: given two elements
x
and
y
,
x
<
y
iff there is a path going upwards that connects
x
to y. For instance, the fact that [1, 1] < [3, 4] is confirmed by the path [1, 1]
→ [2, 2]
→ [3, 4].
But the diagram also serves to show why this relationship is not a strict weak order: for it to be so, incomparable elements (those not connected) should be indistinguishable in that they are connected upwards and downwards with the same elements, and this is clearly not the case (in fact, it is not the case for any pair of incomparable elements). In mathematical terms, our relationship is of a more general type called a
strict partial order
.
Going back to C++, associative containers assume that the elements inserted form a linear arrangement with respect to <: when we try to insert a new element
y
that is incomparable with some previously inserted element
x
, the properties of strict weak orders allows us to determine that
x
and
y
are equivalent, so nothing breaks up (the insertion fails as a duplicate for a
std::map
, or
y
is added next to
x
for a
std::multimap
).
There's a way to accommodate our interval scenario with
std::map
, though. As long as the elements we are inserting belong to the same connecting path or
chain
,
std::map
can't possibly "know" if our relationship is a strict weak order or not: it certainly looks like one for the limited subset of elements it has seen so far. Implementation-wise, we just have to make sure we're not comparing partially overlapping intervals:
struct interval_overlap: std::runtime_error
{
interval_overlap(): std::runtime_error("interval overlap"){}
};
bool operator<(const interval& x, const interval& y)
{
if(x.min == y.min) {
if(x.max != y.max) throw interval_overlap();
return false;
}
else if(x.min < y.min) {
if(x.max >= y.min) throw interval_overlap();
return true;
}
else /* x.min > y.min */
{
if(x.min <= y.max) throw interval_overlap();
return false;
}
}
std::map<interval, std::string> m;
m[{0, 9}] = "ABC";
m[{10, 19}] = "DEF";
m[{5, 14}] = "GHI"; // throws interval_overlap
So, when we try to insert an element that would violate the strict weak ordering constraints (that is, it lies outside the chain connecting the intervals inserted so far), an exception is thrown and no undefined behavior is hit. A strict reading of the standard would not allow this workaround, as it is required that the comparison object for the map induce a strict weak ordering for all possible values of
Key
, not only those in the container (or that is my interpretation, at least): for all practical purposes, though, this works and will foreseeably continue to work for all future revisions of the standard.
Bonus point.
Thanks to
heterogeneous lookup
, we can extend our use case to support lookup for
integers
inside the intervals:
struct less_interval
{
using is_transparent = void;
bool operator()(const interval& x, const interval& y) const
{
// as operator< before
}
bool op

data.title: FMD Android: secure open source alternative to Google's Find My Device
data.author: miles
data.article_summary: 该项目提供了一种安全、开源的设备查找和远程控制方案，类似于Google的Find My Device功能。用户可以通过SMS、即时通讯软件或FMD服务器的网页界面进行设备控制。该项目遵循GNU GPLv3开源许可协议，于2020年10月17日创建，旨在提供一个更隐私保护的替代方案。更多详细信息可查阅其README文件。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过非Google服务实现手机丢失追踪的方案及其局限性

不同观点：
• [gausswho] 支持使用自组方案进行手机丢失追踪，具体是通过GrapheneOS、GpsLogger和Syncthing-Fork等开源工具组合，将定位数据定期发送至家用电脑。他认为这种方法虽然复杂且笨重，但能有效避免使用Google Play服务，并且在手机丢失时通过Dawarich查看位置数据。

• [tetris11] 对[gausswho]的方案表示兴趣，但希望了解更多技术细节，特别是关于如何触发数据传输（例如通过SMS监听或持久化的webhook）。这表明他关注方案的具体实现方式，以及该方案在实际应用中的可行性。

• [sneakerblack] 则持不同意见，认为这种方案无法实现与当前Find My Device（FMD）功能深层次的集成，尤其是利用蓝牙信标在手机“关闭”状态下进行追踪。此外，他指出这种方案可能与需要签名 bootloader 和操作系统的应用（如银行应用）存在兼容性问题，暗示了安全性和功能性之间的权衡。

补充讨论：

data.title: Gaming cancer: How citizen science games could help cure disease
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了利用电子游戏推动科学发现，特别是癌症研究的可能性。作者杰夫·吉田在其书《Gaming Cancer》中提出，游戏能激发人类天生的问题解决能力，而这可以应用于科学研究。通过"公民科学游戏"，普通人可以参与解决复杂的科学问题，如癌症治疗中的挑战。这些游戏不同于传统游戏，它们提出的问题可能没有已知解决方案，玩家通过尝试和创新可能找到新方法。文章举例说明，通过设定明确的成功条件和开放式问题，游戏可以成为推动科学进步的工具，正如历史上许多为公共利益设立的竞赛一样。这种方法有望将大众的创造力用于解决医学难题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕科学问题和电子游戏结合的讨论，包括其吸引力、应用潜力及面临的挑战。

不同观点：
• JimiofEden认为Zachtronics的游戏（如Opus Magnum）虽然类似于编程挑战，但由于其复杂的难题设计和竞争元素，仍然具有很强的吸引力，尤其对工程背景的人来说。他强调游戏的简化问题空间、竞争性和基础的打磨是吸引玩家的关键。

• zeristor对游戏价格提出质疑，认为60美元的定价过高，并提到科学游戏如果能像解决癌症等重大问题那样具有实际价值，将更有意义。他同时表达了对其他社会问题的关注，如饮用水污染。

• RataNova指出，在保持游戏趣味性和科学严谨性之间的平衡是一个挑战，但若能成功结合，不仅对癌症研究，而且对任何需要直觉和创造力的复杂系统研究都有巨大潜力。

• noitpmeder提到EVE Online的Project Discovery作为一个类似的例子，展示了游戏如何结合科学研究，提供了一种玩家参与实际科研的模式。

• ashwinsundar和meindnoch以“Ender's Game”作比喻，讨论游戏在生物学和癌症研究中的潜在应用，暗示通过游戏可以培养出如小说中那样的战略和解决问题的能力。

• MITSardine提出“反向蚂蚁算法”的概念，可能在暗示一种通过模拟自然界中蚂蚁行为来解决复杂问题的游戏机制。

• bob_theslob646批评原文对玩家如何帮助治愈疾病的描述不充分，并分享了一篇更详细解释该项目如何通过游戏界面解决复杂生物问题的文章，强调了人类在模式识别上的优势。

• Almondsetat持怀疑态度，认为大多数人不会喜欢这种“教育性”游戏，因为它们往往过于刻意强调教育目的，而忽视了游戏本身的乐趣，导致玩家失去兴趣。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于科学教育类游戏是否能够兼顾趣味性和教育性。Almondsetat认为这些游戏往往因为过于注重教育目的而失去游戏本身的乐趣，而JimiofEden等玩家则认为如果设计得当，这类游戏仍然具有很强的吸引力。

• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是游戏在科学研究中的实际应用，如EVE Online的Project Discovery和Eterna项目，展示了玩家如何通过游戏参与复杂科学问题的解决。

44549134.article_content:
Gaming Cancer: How Citizen Science Games Could Help Cure Disease
By inviting players to tackle real scientific problems, games can offer a hand in solving medicine’s toughest challenges.
Screenshot from the game Nanocrafter, a synthetic biology game created to educate and entertain players while advancing science.
By: Jeff Yoshimi
A↑
A↓
Off
Bright
Dark
Blues
Gray
BeeLine Reader
uses subtle color gradients to help you read more efficiently.
Consider a gamer playing a game. Maybe one of them is in a room near you right now. You hear periodic outbursts of anger and joy. They’ve been at it for hours. These games might be easy to pick up, but they sure aren’t easy to win. As Atari founder Nolan Bushnell said, “The best games are easy to learn and difficult to master.”
Jeff Yoshimi is the author of “
Gaming Cancer: How Building and Playing Video Games Can Accelerate Scientific Discovery
.”
What is it about humans that keeps us glued to a game console for hours on end? One answer is evolutionary:
We’re natural problem solvers
. This same drive continues to benefit us today.  Scientists, for instance, spend years mastering their fields — writing tedious grant proposals, culturing cells for hours, and enduring decades of training. Their persistence leads to better medicine, better technology, a better world.
Games exploit this evolved tendency; they appeal to the ancient circuitry in us that strives to figure things out. Game designers create a virtual embodiment of some kind of problem-solving situation — escaping an enemy, defeating an opponent, making it to the next level, unlocking a skill — and they make it easy and intuitive to start playing. They lure you in with easy wins and progress. But over time, it gets harder and harder, and in the end, to win, you must thread a narrow path through action space, doing just the right things, in the right order, to achieve your goal.
Games appeal to the ancient circuitry in us that strives to figure things out.
These remarkable parallels can be put to good and surprising use, as I argue in my book, “
Gaming Cancer
.” Cancer remains an unsolved problem, and thousands of scientists worldwide are working diligently to make progress in its treatment. What sequence of actions will lead to a better way to block that channel? How can that cell type be detected in early stages? How can that tumor be targeted without harming healthy cells nearby? What treatment will work to eradicate the tumor without making it resistant to the treatment? Scientists, like game players, must thread an incredibly narrow path through action space, but the situation is far more difficult, and it’s not even known if there is any path at all.
This is precisely what games are designed to do: They present players with a situation and a set of possible actions, then challenge them to find the right sequence to achieve a goal. By leveraging this parallel, we can develop citizen science games and design open challenges that enable everyday people to support scientists on their challenging path. This is the task of citizen science.
The games to be made are not like standard games, where the designers know how the game players’ goals can be achieved. But that’s okay. There have long been genres of games where players did things game designers did not dream of. In fact, that is almost always the case. The creators of chess could not have dreamed of all the innovations the game would inspire. The designers of Pacman and Donkey Kong didn’t even know what the highest possible scores were. In those cases, they at least knew the game could be completed; players simply surprised them with new strategies and record-breaking runs. But some puzzles might not even have known solutions, and that can make them even more motivating.
No one has figured this out before; I can be the first!
So long as the game has clear success conditions, everything else stays the same. We can create games where players attempt to solve problems that have never been solved, utilizing a defined set of tools to engineer something that has never been engineered before.
Consider the following challenge: Build a Lego bridge using a fixed set of pieces to support a large weight. A success condition has been defined, but it’s unclear whether success is achievable. Then open the problem to a crowd, to see if they can discover a solution, or perhaps several solutions. In this way, players can find solutions to a problem that the game designer — or in this case, the challenge designer — was not aware of. (This challenge has actually been done.
In an episode of the TV show Lego Masters
, teams were tasked with building bridges that could hold 1,000 pounds.)
The idea here, however, is to explicitly place an unsolved problem related to a common concern within the context of a challenge or a game. In fact, there is a long history of games and competitions for public good. Modern canning and jarring techniques originated in part from

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：无人机、机器人在未来战争和经济中的作用，以及美国在全球供应链中的地位和战略选择。

不同观点：
• tomComb认为，美国正在犯一个大错误，放弃了电动汽车供应链，这将导致其在无人机和机器人领域的领先地位丧失。他建议美国应与其经济对手合作，建立替代中国供应链的方案，并应加强与加拿大和墨西哥的汽车供应链合作。

• weego指出，美国生产的无人机价格昂贵，因为供应商希望通过大预算合同保证收益。现代战争需要大量一次性使用的廉价无人机，这与传统模式有很大不同。

• dkga强调了海军无人机的重要性，指出乌克兰成功使用无人机对抗黑海舰队，以及哥伦比亚毒枭使用无人机运送毒品。他建议发展小型但强大的海军无人机用于反潜作战，认为这对拥有广大边界的国家至关重要。

• amai对无人机未来表示担忧，引用了Kyiv Independent的文章，暗示无人机面临新的防御系统的挑战。

• lesuorac质疑无人机在长期冲突中的优越性，认为无人机只是低成本、低强度的投射工具，无法单独赢得战争。

• amaelius认为战争胜负取决于制造能力，并断言中国在这方面具有优势。

• instagib认为无人机是战争工具箱中的一种工具，但不是关键因素。他提到GPS拒止区域对无人机的影响，并引用了Archer无人机的生产数据来支持观点。

• clvx支持使用光纤无人机，认为俄罗斯在Kursk战役中的成功证明了这一点。

• ironyman指出，五角大楼已将小型无人机视为“消耗性商品”，但美国军事战略仍以长距离杀伤链为主，不会依赖廉价无人机群。

• dmix批评高昂的巡航导弹成本，认为未来回顾时可能会发现这是不明智的选择。

• wkat4242质疑无人机在实际战争胜利中的作用，认为它们主要用于骚扰而非决定性胜利。

• christkv认为无人机在拥有空中优势的情况下不具优势，只有在无法建立空中霸权时才显得重要，如乌克兰战争。

• more_corn担心中国切断电子产品供应对美国高科技武器供应链的影响，建议主动应对这一挑战。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及美国供应链战略、无人机生产模式转变、海军无人机的潜在应用以及中国在制造能力上的优势。
• 争议焦点在于无人机在现代战争中的实际效果和战略重要性，以及美国在全球竞争中的供应链策略。

data.title: C3 solved memory lifetimes with scopes
data.author: lerno
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了C3语言通过引入Temp分配器和作用域机制解决内存生命周期管理的问题。传统方法如RAII、引用计数和垃圾回收各有优缺点，而C3的Temp分配器结合了这些方法的优点，提供了一种自动且高效的内存管理方案。Temp分配器基于内存分配区域（arenas）的概念，在执行离开其作用域时自动重置，避免了内存泄漏。文章通过代码示例展示了如何使用`@pool()`定义内存可用范围，并通过工具Valgrind验证内存管理的有效性。此外，C3还允许对嵌套作用域的内存清理进行显式控制，提高了灵活性。这种方法兼顾了性能和易用性，无需复杂的RAII或垃圾回收机制。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：C3语言中的内存管理机制（如@pool）与Rust的借用检查器、内存安全、编译时间等技术特点的比较与争议。

不同观点：
• [ameliaquining] 认为Rust的编译速度慢并非主要由于借用检查器，而是由于其他特性（如单态化、LLVM优化、过程宏等）。借用检查器的运行时间是线性的，且在整体编译时间中占比较小。Rust编译器的代码库复杂，改进需要大量资源投入。
• [UncleMeat] 强调借用检查器的核心优势在于确保不能访问已被销毁的内存以及保证不能在其他地方需要常量时改变其内容，而不仅仅是为了防止内存泄漏。
• [hvenev] 质疑讨论内容是否真的与借用检查有关，认为这是关于内存管理的讨论，而不是内存安全。并提出C3中是否能防止返回已被释放的内存的问题。
• [duped] 认为C3并没有解决使用后释放（use-after-free）的问题，只是将其转化为运行时错误。内存泄漏问题在特定类型的程序中是难以解决的，尤其是需要处理资源耗尽的情况。自动垃圾回收是已解决的问题，但C3的机制是否提供了显著不同的语言语义还需证明。
• [unscaled] 认为将内存池与引用计数或借用检查器进行比较是不恰当的。内存池在很多场景下简化了内存管理，但并不能提供内存安全。
• [rq1] 质疑C3的@pool机制是否真的解决了内存生命周期问题，并要求展示在多线程或高吞吐量服务器等复杂场景下的非平凡案例。
• [hrhrdorhrvfbf] 提到Rust的分配器接口不好用，希望看到C3如何处理在临时分配器范围外使用对象引用的问题。
• [smcameron] 认为@pool没有覆盖到一些常见的情况，如线程间内存分配和队列处理。
• [Philpax] 认为"解决"内存生命周期问题的说法过于强烈，C3的机制并不能解决所有情况，特别是不同作用域数据交互时。
• [cogman10] 认为C3的@pool与C++的析构函数和智能指针类似，没有明显优势。
• [Alifatisk] 对C3的机制感到兴趣，并希望看到类似ObjC的@autoreleasepool的实现，也希望D语言能引入类似机制。
• [amelius] 指出智能编译器已经通过逃逸分析实现了类似的优化。
• [timeon] 认为技术文章不需要通过与借用检查器的对比来吸引眼球，直接介绍特性即可。
• [ltbarcly3] 认为如果所有内存分配模式都是词法的，那么这种机制是最简单和明显的，但这并不能解决实际问题。
• [bbminner] 要求提供一个复杂的例子，展示如何在资源管理器中处理指针访问和资源释放问题，认为内存池不足以解决这些问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于C3的内存管理机制是否真的优于Rust的借用检查器，特别是在处理复杂内存生命周期问题和多线程环境下的表现。
• 不同评论者对C3的@pool机制能否解决使用后释放问题和内存泄漏问题持不同看法，部分评论者认为这只是对已有技术的重新包装。
• 一些评论者对C3的机制表示兴趣，并希望看到更多实际应用的例子和与其他语言机制的比较。

The
C3
Blog
Forget Borrow Checkers: C3 Solved Memory Lifetimes With Scopes
2025-07-11
Modern languages offer a variety of techniques to help with dynamic memory management, each one a different tradeoff in terms of performance, control and complexity. In this post we’ll look at an old idea, memory allocation regions or arenas, implemented via the C3 Temp allocator, which is the new default for C3.
The Temp allocator combines the ease of use of garbage collection with C3’s unique features to give a simple and (semi)-automated solution within a manual memory management language. The Temp allocator helps you avoid memory leaks, improve performance, and simplify code compared to traditional approaches.
Memory allocations come in two broad types
stack
allocations which are compact, efficient and automatic and heap allocations which are much larger and have
customisable organisation
. Custom organisation allows both innovation and footguns in equal measure, let’s explore those.
Memory Leaks
When we dynamically allocate memory, with say
malloc()
typically we need to
free()
it afterwards, otherwise we can’t use that memory until the OS process exits. If that memory isn’t being used and it has not been freed this is called a
memory leak
and can lead to restricting or running out of available system memory.
Avoiding Memory Leaks
Common solutions are
RAII
,
reference counting
or
garbage collection
which automatically free those variables.
Each method has different tradeoffs.
RAII
needs classes or structs to manage their own memory cleanup with a lot of extra code.
Reference counting
counts how many users each memory allocation has, when this hits zero the memory is freed. Reference counting is expensive with multiple CPU cores as we need to synchronise these counts and share information between cores.
Garbage collection
competes with the program for both memory and CPU time, reducing program performance and increasing memory usage.
Memory Allocation Regions
Memory allocation regions, go by various names: arenas, pools, contexts; The idea dates back to the 1960’s with the IBM OS/360 mainframes having a similar system. Memory regions are efficient for managing many memory allocations and can be freed in a single operation, and are particularly effective when we know the memory will not be needed later. That is, we know the memory’s lifetime. This idea is powerful and used in many applications like web server request handlers or database transactions, as used by the
Apache webserver
and the
Postgres database
.
Memory allocation regions use a single buffer so have good locality because all the allocations are closely associated together, making it more efficient for CPU access, compared to traditional
malloc
where allocations are spread throughout the heap.
Memory allocation regions may make it easier to manage memory, however you still need to
remember
to free them, and if you forget to do call free, then that memory will still leak.
Enter The Temp Allocator
The Temp allocator in C3 is a region based allocator which is
automatically
reset once execution leaves its scope, so you cannot forget to free the memory and can’t leak memory. The Temp allocator in C3 is a builtin in the standard library, called
@pool()
and using it you can define the scope where the allocated variables are available, for example:
fn
int
example
(
int
input
)
{
@
pool()
{
// Allocate temp_variable on the heap with Temp allocator
int
*
temp_variable
=
mem::tnew(
int
)
;
*
temp_variable
=
56
;
input
=
input
+
temp_variable;
return
input;
};
// Automatically cleanup temp_variable
}
fn
void
main
()
{
int
result
=
example(
1
)
;
assert(result
==
57
,
"
The result should be 57
"
)
;
}
Check With Valgrind
Valgrind is a tool which detects memory leaks and we can use it to show the temp allocator managed the memory for us automatically.
Terminal window
valgrind
./pool_example
|
&
grep
"
All heap blocks were freed
"
==129129==
All
heap
blocks
were
freed
--
no
leaks
are
possible
Success!
We have relatively performant memory allocations managed automatically without needing
RAII
,
garbage collection
or
reference counting
.
Controlling Variable Cleanup
Normally temp allocated variables are cleaned up at the end of the closest
@pool
scope, but what if you have nested
@pool
and want explicit control over when it’s cleaned up? Simple: assign the temp allocator with the scope you need to a variable, and use it explicitly. The temp allocator in a scope is a global variable called
tmem
.
fn String
*
example
(
int
input
)
{
// previous global temp allocator from main() scope
Allocator temp_allocator
=
tmem;
@
pool()
{
// Allocate on the global temp allocator
String
*
returned
=
allocator::new(temp_allocator, String)
;
*
returned
=
string::format(temp_allocator,
"
modified
%s
"
, input)
;
return
returned;
};
}
fn
void
main
()
{
// top-most temp allocator, tmem created here
@
pool()
{
String
*
returned
=
example(
42
)
;
// "modified 42" string returned
io::printn(
*
ret

data.title: Show HN: Learn LLMs LeetCode Style
data.author: Exorust
data.article_summary: TorchLeet是一个用于提升PyTorch和深度学习技能的项目，包含两类问题集：普通问题集和大型语言模型（LLM）问题集。普通问题集涵盖从基础到高级的PyTorch实践问题，如线性回归、卷积神经网络（CNN）、循环神经网络（RNN）、自定义损失函数等。LLM问题集专注于从零实现大型语言模型，包括注意力机制、嵌入、多头注意力等。该项目旨在通过动手实践深入理解PyTorch概念，提供不完整的代码块和解决方案以帮助学习。问题难度从基础到高级，适合不同水平的学习者。

44550157.article_summary: TorchLeet是一个用于提升PyTorch和深度学习技能的项目，包含两类问题集：普通问题集和大型语言模型（LLM）问题集。普通问题集涵盖从基础到高级的PyTorch实践问题，如线性回归、卷积神经网络（CNN）、循环神经网络（RNN）、自定义损失函数等。LLM问题集专注于从零实现大型语言模型，包括注意力机制、嵌入、多头注意力等。该项目旨在通过动手实践深入理解PyTorch概念，提供不完整的代码块和解决方案以帮助学习。问题难度从基础到高级，适合不同水平的学习者。

data.title: Lua beats MicroPython for embedded devs
data.author: willhschmid
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Lua与MicroPython在嵌入式开发中的优劣比较

不同观点：
• Lua作为嵌入式开发策略优于MicroPython：一些评论者（如[1vuio0pswjnm7]和[delduca]）引用多个来源和个人经验，认为Lua在速度和嵌入性上优于MicroPython。他们提到Lua更小、更快，并且Toit语言声称比MicroPython快30倍。此外，Lua的嵌入式开发策略被认为更容易集成和使用。
• MicroPython的扩展性和易用性：[jononor]认为文章对MicroPython的批评不准确，指出MicroPython可以通过C轻松扩展，并且可以使用如ulab之类的库来实现类似Python的功能。此外，文章中提到的一些限制（如无法使用numpy）被认为是不准确的。
• MicroPython和Lua的应用场景不同：[10000truths]指出MicroPython和Lua解决的是不同的问题。MicroPython旨在取代传统的C运行时，适用于嵌入式平台，而Lua则更适合作为嵌入式应用中的脚本语言。
• Lua和MicroPython的实用性争议：[KaiserPro]认为Lua和MicroPython都有其局限性，Lua需要自行支持工具链，而MicroPython虽然适合网络应用，但在精确控制和安全性上不如C/C++。
• 对"严肃开发者"使用脚本语言的质疑：[ycombinatrix]和[Palomides]质疑是否真的有"严肃的"嵌入式开发者使用MicroPython或Lua，暗示编译语言可能是更常见的选择。

补充讨论：
• 其他嵌入式脚本语言的推荐：[theoutfield]提到AngelScript作为一种被低估的嵌入式脚本语言，容易扩展且是C/C++的子集。[analog31]询问如何在Arduino开发环境中尝试Lua，而[jokoon]则表达了对Lua语法的不满，更偏好gdscript。
• 开发体验和类型提示：[smohare]提到对Lua的动态特性和缺乏类型提示感到困惑，认为这与Python类似，对专业代码审查来说是个认知障碍。

争议焦点：
• Lua与MicroPython在嵌入式开发中的实际性能和应用场景优劣是主要的争议点。一方认为Lua更小更快，适合嵌入式开发，另一方则认为MicroPython的扩展性和易用性使其在某些场景下更具优势。
• 对"严肃开发者"是否使用这些脚本语言的质疑，反映了在嵌入式开发领域中对脚本语言实用性的不同看法。

总结：评论主要围绕Lua和MicroPython在嵌入式开发中的性能、应用场景和实用性展开讨论，并涉及其他脚本语言的推荐和开发体验的分享。争议点主要集中在两者的实际应用效果和开发者对其的接受程度。

data.title: The North Korean fake IT worker problem is ubiquitous
data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了北韩假冒IT求职者对企业的威胁，以及如何识别和阻止这些骗局。多家美国和欧洲公司发现，许多看似优秀的求职者实际上使用虚假身份，目的是窃取公司源代码和敏感数据，甚至进行勒索。这些假求职者的特征包括简历丰富但LinkedIn连接少、拒绝面对面面试、使用深伪视频等。企业高管指出，这些骗子可能已经渗透到许多大公司中，利用远程工作机会进行诈骗。为应对这一问题，企业需加强身份验证，警惕可疑求职者，并通过技术手段如ChatGPT比对面试回答的一致性来识别潜在骗局。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕虚假IT工作者（特别是来自朝鲜的）通过伪造LinkedIn档案获得工作的讨论，涉及身份验证、背景调查和可能的解决方案。

不同观点：
• **虚假LinkedIn档案和黑客攻击的真实案例**：croemer分享了其同事LinkedIn账号被黑，档案被篡改为朝鲜背景的实例，强调了虚假档案问题的严重性，并指出检测这种变化的困难。
  
• **美国与欧洲雇主的背景调查差异**：mkl95指出，美国公司通常会进行严格的背景调查，但欧洲公司则未必，这使得虚假工作者更容易渗透进欧洲企业。

• **技术手段在虚假工作者问题中的应用**：Maxious提到FBI对微型KVM设备（虚假工作者使用的一种工具）的关注，而 CyberMacGyver 则提到自己正在开发免费服务来解决这一问题，并声称自2018年以来已经标记了数千个虚假申请者。

• **强制性面对面入职作为解决方案**：Havoc建议通过强制第一周入职时进行面对面的方式来解决虚假身份问题，ta1243对此表示支持，认为通过团队互动可以很快发现不一致。

• **政治与外国情报渗透的深层次威胁**：jongjong提出，某些国家的科技行业可能正在被外国情报机构渗透，尤其是那些拥有大量外籍工程师的国家，如澳大利亚。jongjong进一步推测，某些国家可能通过在关键公司安插人员来获取政治利益。

• **失业开发者与虚假工作者问题**：giantg2指出，目前有许多失业的开发者，虚假工作者问题使得合法求职者更难找到工作，并建议像Pearson这样的公司设立验证面试中心来解决这一问题。

• **对虚假工作者问题夸大的质疑**：abxyz认为，所谓的朝鲜虚假工作者问题可能被夸大，并指出某些公司（如Socure）可能通过夸大问题来推销自己的解决方案。abxyz进一步指出，许多被标记为“朝鲜”的申请者实际上可能只是来自贫困国家的人试图获得工作。

• **政府提供在线身份验证服务的可能性**：dakiol建议政府提供简单的在线身份验证服务，以解决虚假身份问题，而Barrin92则质疑虚假工作者是否真的仅通过伪造LinkedIn档案就能通过所有法律和财务审核。

• **对公开讨论和解决方案的反思**：alganet认为，这种公开讨论可能反而助长了不必要的恐慌，并指出这种问题应该直接告知相关公司或通过私下调查解决。alganet还提到，需要采取措施减少虚假工作者可利用的工具，但这些措施可能会对某些技术发展造成影响。

补充讨论：
- **幽默与讽刺**：belter以讽刺的口吻指出，正当本地开发者难以找到工作时，虚假朝鲜IT工作者却轻松获得职位，暗示对现状的无奈。
- **利用政治敏感问题进行身份验证**：conradev提到，可以通过要求申请者批评朝鲜领导人来鉴别其真实性，这是一种非正式但可能有效的方法。

争议焦点：虚假工作者问题的严重性及其背后的政治动机。jongjong和abxyz的观点形成了鲜明对比，前者认为这是一个深层次的政治渗透问题，而后者认为这是被夸大的经济问题。

Cyber-crime
10
You have a fake North Korean IT worker problem - here's how to stop it
10
Thick resumes with thin LinkedIn connections are one sign. Refusing an in-person interview is another
Jessica Lyons
Sun 13 Jul 2025
//
11:02 UTC
By now, the North Korean fake IT worker problem is so ubiquitous that if you think you don't have any phony resumes or imposters in your interview queue, you're asleep at the wheel.
"Almost every CISO of a Fortune 500 company that I've spoken to — I'll just characterize as dozens that I've spoken to — have admitted that they had a North Korean IT worker problem,"
said
Mandiant Consulting CTO Charles Carmakal during a threat-intel roundtable, admitting that even Mandiant's parent company Google is not immune.
"We have seen this in our own pipelines," added Iain Mulholland, Google Cloud's senior director of security engineering.
"We've certainly seen applicants that fit into this category with various IOCs [indicators of compromise] that we've shared with partners and peers," Snowflake CISO Brad Jones told
The Register
.
These types of scams, largely originating from North Korea, or at least funneling money back to Pyongyang, have cost American businesses at least
$88 million over six years
, the Department of Justice said last year.
In some cases, the fraudsters use their insider access to steal proprietary source code and other sensitive data, and then extort their employers with threats to leak corporate data if not
paid a ransom demand
.
As US-based companies become more aware of the fake IT worker problem, the job seekers are increasingly
targeting European employers
, too.
Nearly all executives who spoke to
The Register
in recent months have seen a flood of these types of applicants applying for open positions, most of them in engineering and software development, and all of them remote work.
In some instances, the scammers even used deepfake videos in attempts to get hired, including at a security company that uses AI to find vulnerabilities in code. "If they almost fooled me, a cybersecurity expert, they definitely fooled some people," Vidoc Security Lab co-founder Dawid Moczadło told us in an
earlier interview
.
"We believe, at this point, every Fortune 100 and potentially Fortune 500 have a pretty high number of risky employees on their books," Socure Chief Growth Officer Rivka Little told us.
Using a fake identity…to apply for an identity job
Over the past few months, Socure has seen a ton of fake candidates applying for open jobs, according to Little, who has been leading the charge on the IT worker scam front. This seems an especially ironic choice for employment scammers, because Socure provides identity verification services to other companies.
For a senior engineering role, Socure used to receive between 150 and 200 applications over three or four months. That number has recently jumped to more than 1,999 purported job seekers in a two-month period. At least some of those extra applicants have weirdly suspicious profiles.
"We were in our executive meeting one Monday morning, and our chief people officer said, 'We're getting these super-strange resumes. They don't seem to be connected to people who are valid. This feels like a fake identity,'" Little said. "There were just too many disconnects."
Chief among these disconnects were "shallow" LinkedIn profiles paired with "beefy resumes," she explained, citing job-seeker claims of working at Meta, attending Ivy League schools, developing major tech companies' flagship products … but then only having 25 LinkedIn connections.
Once the recruitment team began meeting via video conferences with some of the applicants, they noted extremely Western-sounding names, like James Anderson, paired with East Asian appearances and accented English, in much higher numbers than they expected.
He was affable, a nice guy. He was making jokes. There was nothing about him that would make me not want to work with him
"You can't profile people, so with the first few we were like, that's interesting. But then when it was 10, 20, 30 — this is implausible at that rate and number, demographically," Little said. "We decided to follow through on a couple of candidates to really suss out what is going on here, and also to allow us to capture consent, because you can't really dig into someone's identity background unless you have consent to do so."
In all of these cases, Little's team noted a number of oddities: new-ish email addresses, phone numbers that didn't match claimed geographic locations, routing everything through a VPN, and educational backgrounds that didn't check out.
Little said she fed a handful of job applicant questions into ChatGPT and saved the chatbot's responses for reference during the interview.
"If his answers are anywhere close to these, then we'll also know there's a problem, and that's exactly what happened," she said. "It was insane."

• **技术手段在虚假工作者问题中的应用**：Maxious提到FBI对微型KVM设备（虚假工作者使用的一种工具）的关注，而 CyberMacGyver 则提到自己正在开发免费服务来解决这一问题，并声称自2018年以来已经标记了数千个虚假申请者。

• **强制性面对面入职作为解决方案**：Havoc建议通过强制第一周入职时进行面对面的方式来解决虚假身份问题，ta1243对此表示支持，认为通过团队互动可以很快发现不一致。

• **政治与外国情报渗透的深层次威胁**：jongjong提出，某些国家的科技行业可能正在被外国情报机构渗透，尤其是那些拥有大量外籍工程师的国家，如澳大利亚。jongjong进一步推测，某些国家可能通过在关键公司安插人员来获取政治利益。

• **失业开发者与虚假工作者问题**：giantg2指出，目前有许多失业的开发者，虚假工作者问题使得合法求职者更难找到工作，并建议像Pearson这样的公司设立验证面试中心来解决这一问题。

• **对虚假工作者问题夸大的质疑**：abxyz认为，所谓的朝鲜虚假工作者问题可能被夸大，并指出某些公司（如Socure）可能通过夸大问题来推销自己的解决方案。abxyz进一步指出，许多被标记为“朝鲜”的申请者实际上可能只是来自贫困国家的人试图获得工作。

• **政府提供在线身份验证服务的可能性**：dakiol建议政府提供简单的在线身份验证服务，以解决虚假身份问题，而Barrin92则质疑虚假工作者是否真的仅通过伪造LinkedIn档案就能通过所有法律和财务审核。

• **对公开讨论和解决方案的反思**：alganet认为，这种公开讨论可能反而助长了不必要的恐慌，并指出这种问题应该直接告知相关公司或通过私下调查解决。alganet还提到，需要采取措施减少虚假工作者可利用的工具，但这些措施可能会对某些技术发展造成影响。

补充讨论：
- **幽默与讽刺**：belter以讽刺的口吻指出，正当本地开发者难以找到工作时，虚假朝鲜IT工作者却轻松获得职位，暗示对现状的无奈。
- **利用政治敏感问题进行身份验证**：conradev提到，可以通过要求申请者批评朝鲜领导人来鉴别其真实性，这是一种非正式但可能有效的方法。

争议焦点：虚假工作者问题的严重性及其背后的政治动机。jongjong和abxyz的观点形成了鲜明对比，前者认为这是一个深层次的政治渗透问题，而后者认为这是被夸大的经济问题。

data.title: Monitoring My Homelab, Simply
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种简化的家庭实验室监控方案，作者开发了一个小型程序来进行HTTP、DNS、TLS等检测，并通过https://ntfy.sh发送通知。该方案旨在满足以下需求：出现严重故障时通知、持续故障时重复提醒、修复后通知以及易于添加检测器。程序通过一个循环运行检测器，失败时发送通知，并每小时提醒一次。作者提供了TLS检测器的示例代码，并说明了如何处理故障和恢复通知。程序设计简单，避免复杂的状态管理，且易于部署和维护。作者的目标是捕捉明显的系统问题，而非解决所有潜在故障或提供详尽的历史数据分析。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：各类监控解决方案的比较与选择

不同观点：
• reboot81 推荐使用 https://healthchecks.io 并提供了针对不同操作系统（Windows、MacOS、Linux）的脚本链接，强调其易用性。
• Jedd 提到使用两个“死开关”（dead man switches）进行监控，并通过个人经历强调日志聚合的重要性，指出家庭实验室中日志聚合的简便性及其潜在的多重好处。
• Evidlo 推荐使用 updown.io，因其价格低廉且易于使用，特别适合单台机器的监控。
• Scaevolus 使用 Prometheus + Prometheus Alertmanager 组合，强调其功能丰富和报警表达式的可视化优势，且可通过容器化简化部署。
• danesparza 强调家庭实验室中应监控的具体指标，如RAID健康状态、磁盘空间、备份作业运行情况和SSL证书到期等。
• justusthane 计划开发一个Python程序作为监控解决方案，强调其可扩展性和插件化设计，但提到开发进度缓慢。
• Havoc 认为 Uptime Kuma 最简单，尤其因为其提供了Python API包，便于批量操作和编辑。
• compumike 自荐其团队开发的监控和报警解决方案 https://heiioncall.com/，强调其功能全面和灵活的静音设置。
• bonobocop 推荐 Cloudprober，因其易于配置和扩展，适合与Go语言集成。
• Spooky23 使用 node exporter 到 Prometheus 和 Grafana 的组合，并通过 Uptime Kuma 和 Pushover 实现报警，强调其易于设置和实用性。
• JZL003 使用 Node Express 服务器结合多个免费监控服务进行监控，通过Promise.all管理状态，并利用免费监控服务发送邮件报警。
• frenchtoast8 在工作中使用 Datadog，但认为其对于家庭实验室过于昂贵，推荐 NewRelic 和 Grafana Cloud 的免费计划，但指出学习成本问题。
• loloquwowndueo 质疑 reboot81 的方案是否重新发明了 Monit，并提到 Prometheus + Alertmanager 的Docker容器化部署简单且稳定。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是解决方案的复杂性和成本之间的平衡。例如，Jedd 和 frenchtoast8 强调了高成本工具如 Datadog 在家庭实验室中的不适用性，而 Evidlo 和 Havoc 则推荐了更廉价且易用的替代方案。
• 另一个讨论点是日志聚合和历史数据的重要性，Jedd 通过个人经历强调了这一点，而其他评论者如 Spooky23 则通过具体案例说明了监控系统的实际效益。
• 可扩展性和易用性也是重要讨论点，justusthane 提出的自定义Python程序和 Havoc 对 Uptime Kuma 的API批量操作的推荐都反映了这一点。

总体而言，讨论围绕监控工具的选择展开，涉及成本、功能、易用性和扩展性等多个方面。

data.title: Does showing seconds in the system tray actually use more power?
data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Windows系统在任务栏显示秒数对能耗的影响及其技术实现

不同观点：
• **优化能耗的观点**：一些用户如[gleenn]和[renewiltord]提到，每秒更新一次时间显示会导致电池续航显著下降，甚至达到13%的电量损失。他们认为这种优化是有必要的，尤其是在便携设备上，需要尽量减少不必要的屏幕更新以节省电量。[lxgr]补充说，桌面操作系统通常不像智能手机或可穿戴设备那样针对静态屏幕内容进行能耗优化，但也许可以借鉴这些设备的硬件设计。

• **对微软技术能力的质疑**：[DecentShoes]和[Jaxan]对微软的技术能力提出质疑，认为微软拥有大量资源，却无法实现像十年前Windows 10那样简单的功能（如点击时钟显示秒数）。[Jaxan]进一步指出，微软在节能问题上存在双重标准，一方面推卸秒数显示的责任，另一方面系统却进行大量浪费资源的操作（如广告、网络请求等）。

• **不需要秒数显示的观点**：[rwallace]认为秒数显示是“反特性”，会不断吸引用户的注意力，因此最好不显示秒数，以减少不必要的干扰，符合节能和专注的需求。

• **技术解决方案的讨论**：[alok-g]和[DoctorOetker]从技术角度讨论了如何优化秒数显示的能耗问题。[alok-g]提到硬件加速和渲染小区域像素不应该消耗太多资源。[DoctorOetker]则提出了一种更高效的实现方式，通过预先存储字体和颜色等信息，避免上下文切换，以极小的开销实现秒数更新。

• **其他硬件优化的建议**：[albert_e]提出了一种架构上的设想，即使用一个低功耗的辅助CPU处理像秒数显示这样的简单任务，让主CPU进入低功耗状态，以达到节能的效果。[seanalltogether]则建议在测试中增加轻量级的浏览器操作，以便更全面地评估能耗影响。

• **对整个讨论的调侃**：[fkrkrkgkgk]对讨论本身进行了调侃，认为在面对像GeForce 5090这样高功耗的硬件时，秒数显示的能耗问题显得微不足道。

补充讨论：
• **物理学角度的分析**：[__MatrixMan__]从物理学角度解释了Landauer's principle，指出每次更新时间显示时都会产生一定的热量和能耗，尽管这种影响非常微小，但仍然存在。

• **实际操作中的选择**：[endorphine]提到在Linux系统中配置秒数显示时，也考虑过能耗问题，并选择禁用秒数显示，认为即使是微小的能耗节省也是值得的。

争议的焦点：微软是否应该为秒数显示功能做出优化，以及如何在技术上实现这种优化以平衡能耗和用户需求。

data.title: Show HN: A Raycast-compatible launcher for Linux
data.author: ByteAtATime
data.article_summary:
**Raycast-Linux** 是一个为 Linux 开发的、受 Raycast 启发的开源启动器。它旨在重现 Raycast 的核心功能，包括可扩展命令面板、支持 Raycast API 的扩展、智能计算器（由 SoulverCore 驱动）、剪贴板历史记录、文本片段和 AI 集成等。由于 macOS 和 Linux 之间的差异，部分 Raycast 扩展可能不兼容，尤其是依赖 macOS 特有 API 或二进制文件的扩展。

用户可以通过 GitHub Releases 页面下载最新的 **.AppImage** 文件，并通过命令行赋予执行权限后运行。该应用需要 glibc 2.38 及以上版本，并建议 Wayland 用户配置 udev 规则以启用全局文本片段功能。若要从源代码构建，需安装 Rust、Node.js、pnpm、Tauri 及 Swift 工具链。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Linux平台上的Raycast替代品及其相关技术讨论

不同观点：
• Imustaskforhelp认为该AppImage文件过大，与其预期不符，特别是考虑到Tauri框架本应带来更小的体积。此外，他在Wayland环境下遇到EGL显示错误，并表示自己使用dmenu（fuzzel）和自定义键绑定（hyprland）作为替代方案。
• runjake对项目表示赞赏，但建议更改名称以避免潜在的商标问题。他还提到其他可扩展的Linux启动器，如KRunner和Albert。
• a022311对项目表示高度赞赏，并建议使用Deno作为运行时以解决扩展启动慢的问题，同时推荐Numbat作为Soulver计算器的替代方案，以及参考Project Gauntlet项目。
• ksynwa引用了维基百科上关于Raycast的定义，强调其最初是为macOS开发的。
• mynegation和flipcoder都提到名称问题，认为可能会引发法律纠纷，建议尽快更改名称。
• jraph提到KRunner作为另一个可扩展的Linux启动器选项。
• Sophira关注Wayland环境下的安全问题，质疑添加udev规则是否会削弱Wayland对键盘访问的保护机制。
• _seiryuu_表示项目在cosmic shell环境下表现有些异常，但在其他环境下运行良好。
• imcritic对项目的价值提出质疑，认为增加更多软件未必能显著提升效率。
• ddaletski和hiyer都表示自己正在开发类似的项目，但看到该项目后考虑贡献代码而不是继续自己的项目。
• evertedsphere的评论较为调侃，没有提供实质性意见。

Raycast for Linux
An open-source, Raycast-inspired launcher for Linux.
For more background on this project, I have a
post here
.
Disclaimer:
This is a hobby project and is
not
affiliated with, nor endorsed by, the official Raycast team.
✨ Features
This launcher aims to recreate most of Raycast's core features on Linux:
Extensible Command Palette
: The core of the application. Search for and launch applications, run commands, execute quicklinks, and more.
Extension Support
: Run extensions built Raycast's API. Features a built-in store to browse and install extensions from the official Raycast Store.
Powerful Calculator
: A smart calculator integrated directly into the search bar, powered by
SoulverCore
. It handles unit conversions, currency, and complex math expressions.
Clipboard History
: A searchable history of everything you've copied, with support for text, images, links, and colors.
Snippets
: Create and manage text snippets that can be expanded anywhere on your system. Supports dynamic placeholders for dates, clipboard content, and more.
AI Integration
: Connects to OpenRouter to bring the power of various AI models directly into the launcher.
And more
to come!
🧩 Extension Compatibility
While the goal is to support a wide range of Raycast extensions, there are some inherent limitations due to the differences between macOS and Linux. Common reasons an extension might not work include:
macOS-specific APIs
: Many extensions rely on native macOS features like AppleScript (
runAppleScript
), hardcoded paths (
/Applications/
), or specific system libraries that do not exist on Linux.
Native Binaries
: Extensions that bundle pre-compiled binaries for macOS will not work. Similarly, extensions that use Swift to interact with the operating system won't work either.
Assumed Permissions
: Extensions may assume they have access to macOS-specific permissioned data (like Contacts or Calendars) which have no direct equivalent.
🚀 Installation
You can download the latest release from the
GitHub Releases page
.
Currently, only an
.AppImage
is provided. After downloading, make it executable:
chmod +x
<
downloaded-file-name
>
.AppImage
./
<
downloaded-file-name
>
.AppImage
This will open a long-running process in the background. To toggle the visibility of the window, simply run it again.
Depending on your environment, you may be able to bind the script to a hotkey. For example, on Hyprland:
bind = ALT, Space, exec, /path/to/raycast-linux.AppImage
System Requirements
The application requires
glibc
version
2.38
, which is installed by default on Ubuntu 24.04, Fedora 40, and recent versions of Arch Linux.
Wayland users:
For the global snippet expansion feature to work, the application needs permission to read keyboard events. The recommended and most secure method is to add a
udev
rule.
Create the
udev
rule file:
sudo nano /etc/udev/rules.d/99-raycast-linux.rules
Add the following line to the file:
This rule grants the user at the physical console access to keyboard devices.
KERNEL=="event*", ENV{ID_INPUT_KEYBOARD}=="1", TAG+="uaccess"
Reload the
udev
rules to apply the changes:
sudo udevadm control --reload-rules
&&
sudo udevadm trigger
🛠️ Building from Source
If you prefer to build the project from its source code, you'll need to set up the development environment.
Prerequisites
Rust
: Install via
rustup
.
Node.js
: Use a recent LTS version.
pnpm
is the package manager for this project (
npm i -g pnpm
).
Tauri Prerequisites
: Follow the official
Tauri guide
to install system dependencies.
Swift Toolchain
: The calculator feature uses a Swift wrapper around SoulverCore.
Installation & Running
Clone the repository:
git clone https://github.com/ByteAtATime/raycast-linux.git
cd
raycast-linux
Install dependencies:
This project uses a pnpm workspace. Install all dependencies from the root directory.
pnpm install
Build the Node.js sidecar binary:
This step compiles the JavaScript plugin hos
44551762.article_summary:
**Raycast-Linux** 是一个为 Linux 开发的、受 Raycast 启发的开源启动器。它旨在重现 Raycast 的核心功能，包括可扩展命令面板、支持 Raycast API 的扩展、智能计算器（由 SoulverCore 驱动）、剪贴板历史记录、文本片段和 AI 集成等。由于 macOS 和 Linux 之间的差异，部分 Raycast 扩展可能不兼容，尤其是依赖 macOS 特有 API 或二进制文件的扩展。

data.title: How does a screen work?
data.author: chkhd
data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要介绍了屏幕如何显示图像和颜色。屏幕上的图像是由许多小点（像素）组成的，每个像素又由三个子像素（红、绿、蓝）构成。通过调节这三个颜色的亮度，像素可以呈现出各种颜色。屏幕通过控制每个像素的显示，组合成完整的图像。这种色彩生成方式被称为RGB色彩模型，是电子显示器（如电视、电脑、手机屏幕）普遍采用的技术。文章还提到，人眼无法分辨单独的像素，因此看到的图像是平滑和连续的。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：显示技术（CRT与现代显示器）及相关技术细节

不同观点：
• **perching_aix** 认为现代显示器（LCD和OLED）虽然整个屏幕区域一直亮着，但刷新通常是逐行进行的，而不是全局同时刷新。他建议可以通过慢动作录制智能手机屏幕来观察这种扫描式刷新。
• **LocalH** 指出CRT显示器不显示离散的像素，而是显示离散的扫描线，分辨率取决于显示设备的数模转换器（DAC）和CRT内部硬件。他还提到，即使是"数字RGB"也不是真正的数字信号，因为CRT的电子枪有上升和下降时间，不是瞬时的。

补充讨论：
• **qwertox** 对网页的互动效果和视觉设计表示赞赏，特别是图像缩放时的动态效果和右侧的标尺。
• **Sharlin** 认为CRT显示器作为一种模拟技术，比其数字 successor 更酷，将CRT比作一种"粒子加速器"。
• **retrac** 也认为CRT有某种魔力，图像实际上是一种错觉。如果眼睛足够快，可以看到单个亮点绘制光栅图案。
• **massung** 和 **nu11ptr** 则对链接内容的预期产生误解，前者以为是关于足球战术分析，后者以为是关于终端程序"screen"。
• **killjoywashere** 通过显微镜观察了自己的Pixel 9屏幕，发现不同颜色层的移动速度不同。
• **ksec** 讨论了LCD和OLED的优缺点，提到即将推出的RGB LED背光LCD和磷光蓝OLED技术。
• **YZF** 提到可以用放大镜观察LCD屏幕的子像素排列，并分享了自己曾参与制造LCD彩色滤光片机器的经验。
• **fabiensanglard** 对网页上的绘图工具感兴趣，想要了解使用的具体工具。
• **ekunazanu** 和 **apricot** 对网站内容表示赞赏，期待未来文章。
• **stalco** 对网站的音效有独特感受，提到声音让他以为自己鼻窦有问题。
• **vojtechrichter** 简单表达了对网站设计和未来内容的期待。

争议焦点：
• **现代显示器的刷新方式**：perching_aix 主张现代显示器逐行刷新，而一般认为整个屏幕是同时刷新的。这是一个技术细节上的争议点。
• **CRT与数字显示器的区别**：LocalH 强调CRT显示器的非数字特性，与一般认知中数字显示器的区别。

其他讨论点：
• 网站设计和互动效果（qwertox, fabiensanglard, ekunazanu, apricot, vojtechrichter）
• 对显示技术的个人观察和经验分享（killjoywashere, YZF, ksec）
• 对网站音效的独特体验（stalco）

这些观点展示了参与者对显示技术细节的关注，以及对网站设计和内容的赞赏。

data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何在macOS上利用本地聊天机器人获取FreeBSD相关信息。主要步骤包括：首先安装Ollama和Open-WebUI，然后下载并构建FreeBSD文档，将其上传至Open-WebUI知识库，创建一个基于FreeBSD的模型工作空间，最后开始聊天。强调不应建立官方的chat.freebsd.org，而是使用本地聊天机器人，以满足用户、管理员和开发者的个性化需求。同时提醒，输入的数据应结构良好，以确保机器人提供精确答案。
data.comments_summary:

• JKCalhoun：对在Wikipedia上实现类似RAG的系统表现出兴趣，并提出是否已有现成系统的疑问。他还用幽默的方式将自己设想中的项目比作《银河系百科全书》或《地球及其居民指南》（戏仿《银河系漫游指南》）。

• alexey-salmin：关注点转向技术细节，表达希望解决在FreeBSD上为KDE2打补丁的问题，话题有所偏离主要讨论点。

44550450.article_content:
Out of multiple conversations with people at BSD conferences, I noticed that many would love to see a chatbot that provides precise information on FreeBSDâfor users, admins, and developers.
I strongly believe that there should
not
be an official
chat.freebsd.org
. Local chatbots work well and can be tweaked to fit personal needs.
This documentation is written for macOS with Apple Silicon (because of the GPU support), but should work on other OSes as well.
Step 1: Install Ollama (API for Multiple LLMs)
brew install ollama
ollama pull gemma3:latest
You can try deepseek-r1:latest or even deepseek-r1:70b on more powerful GPUs.
Step 2: Install Open-WebUI for a UI and Built-in Vector Database
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
DATA_DIR=~/.open-webui uvx --python 3.11 open-webui@latest serve
Now browse to http://localhost:5000/
Welcome to your own, local chatbot!
Step 3: Feed Knowledge to the Model
This is where the real work begins:
You need to tell the LLM what’s right or wrong, what’s necessary, and how FreeBSD differs from Linux.
3.1 Download the FreeBSD Documentation
Follow this guide for more details.
Install dependencies (use apt, yum etc. according to your OS):
brew install hugo ruby git bmake
Update your shell configuration:
echo 'export PATH="$(brew --prefix ruby)/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.zshrc
echo 'export PATH="$(brew --prefix hugo)/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.zshrc
echo 'export GEM_PATH="$(gem environment gemdir)"' >> ~/.zshrc
echo 'export PATH="${GEM_PATH}/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.zshrc
source ~/.zshrc
Install required gems:
sudo gem install rouge asciidoctor asciidoctor-pdf asciidoctor-epub3
Clone and build the FreeBSD documentation:
git clone https://git.FreeBSD.org/doc.git ~/doc
cd ~/doc/documentation
bmake run USE_RUBYGEMS=YES RUBY_CMD=$(brew --prefix ruby)/bin/ruby
More information can be found here:
https://docs.freebsd.org/en/books/fdp-primer/overview/#mac-os-installation-process
3.2 Upload Documentation to Open-WebUI
Go to: http://localhost:5000/workspace/knowledge
Click +
Add a knowledge base called "FreeBSD Official Docs"
Add the folder: ~/doc/documentation/public/en/books
3.3 Create a Model Workspace
Go to: http://127.0.0.1:5000/workspace/models
Add a new workspace called "FreeBSD Helper"
Base Model: gemma3:latest
(Or whatever you downloaded via `ollama pull`)
System Prompt
Your are a bot that helps to use, administrate and develop everything that has to do with FreeBSD.
You give technical responses and be very precise. Make sure you use proper FreeBSD tools and don't mistake it with Linux.
You online use the knowledge provided.
Select Knowledge: “FreeBSD Official Docs”
Step 4: Chat Away
Now open a new chat window and select “FreeBSD Helper” as your model.
You might be tempted to add more data, but remember:
The more unstructured the data, the more likely the LLM will give poor results.
E. g. if you give it your PDF invoices it will just fail.
(There are tool for parsing them correctly, but that's not part of this post. Wouldn't fit into 10 posts :-) )
You can use the slider on the top left and lower the value Temperature, this will give you more precise answers.
The hardest part is getting the source data into proper shapeâwhich, thankfully, has already been done by the amazing FreeBSD documentation team.

data.title: A Mental Model for C++ Coroutine
data.author: uvdn7
data.article_summary:
C++中的协程并非像`std::vector`这样的现成库，也不是可以像Rust的`Future` trait那样由用户或库作者实现的特性。C++协程是一个规范，定义了一系列定制点，供库作者实现以构建功能性协程。协程支持操作包括调用、返回、挂起、恢复和销毁。C++协程通过`Task<T>`返回类型进行定制，其中包含`promise_type`，用于定义协程的行为和状态。

`promise_type`可以定制协程的初始调用、返回前、销毁前等行为，并存储协程帧的状态。协程的挂起和恢复通过`co_await`、`co_yield`等实现，用户可以自定义挂起行为以实现后续恢复。C++协程提供了极大的灵活性，可以实现如Rust的`Future`那样的轮询语义，同时支持更多定制化操作。

44534809.article_content:
C++ coroutine is not a library that is ready to go (e.g.
std::vector
). It is not even a trait (think of Rust’s
Future
trait) that library writers or users can implement (or the compiler generates for you in the case of Rust). C++ coroutine is a specification that defines a set of customization points that library writers implement in order to get a functional coroutine.
A function supports two operations -
call
and
return
. A coroutine (in any language) is a generalization of a function. It supports
suspend
,
resume
, and
destroy
in addition of
call
and
return
1
. By this definition, C++ coroutine, Rust Future, are both coroutines. C++ coroutine provides customization points around
call
,
return
,
suspend
, and
resume
; it exposes a handle that allows users to explicitly
destroy
a coroutine as well.
Example
Here is what a potential coroutine
add
could look like. All it does is sleep one second, add two numbers and return the result.
add
should suspend at
co_await
and resume execution once
co_sleep(1)
completes.
Task<int32_t> add(int32_t a, int32_t b) {
uint32_t actualSleepSec = co_await co_sleep(1);
co_return a + b;
}
Task<uint32_t> co_sleep(uint32_t sec) {
// ...
}
Similar to many other languages, the presence of the keyword
co_await
signals that
add
is a coroutine. Let us pretend to be a compiler for a second, the only thing that can be used to customize the behavior of the coroutine is really just the return type
Task<T>
. And indeed that is where C++ extracts the
promise_type
to start the customization process. We will cover more about the
promise_type
later in the post.
The Obvious/Rust Approach
An obvious option here is to make
Task<T>
a subclass of some language defined interface (which owns the coroutine frame
2
for storing state across
co_await
points), where a set of customization points can be implemented as member functions to specify the behavior of this coroutine. If we lump everything into a single class (
Task<T>
in this case),
resume
, will be part of the public interface as well (usually
suspend
only takes place at well defined await points), as one need to be able to resume the coroutine somehow, just like Rust’s
Future::poll
. How does a coroutine know it is ready to be resumed? In Rust’s case, it essentially passes a callback to the
Future
. The callback will resume (
poll
) the
Future
when its dependency is satisfied. In our example, the callback will resume the
add
coroutine after
co_sleep
is complete. But it still needs to somehow pass the return value from
co_sleep
to the caller. Rust solves this problem by passing the callback all the way from the top-most
Future
to the bottom
Future
, and whenever the state changes (because e.g. a network reply is received), it invokes the callback to reschedule the entire Future chain. In our example, the return value from
co_await co_sleep(1);
will be acquired on the next
poll
on
add
. This is a good way of modeling async computation. C++’s coroutine spec, which we will see in a minute, is way more flexible. Actually it is so flexible that we can implement Rust Future’s poll-based semantics (barring the compile transformation of each Future’s state machine) with C++ coroutine.
C++ Coroutine philosophy
Flexibility - it allows one to customize every coroutine operation in meaningful ways. Most importantly,
what happens when a coroutine is first called
what happens before a coroutine returns a value
what happens right before a coroutine reaches the end of its lifetime
when one wants to destroy a coroutine
what happens after a coroutine is suspended
what happens before a coroutine is resumed
So each coroutine can have its own unique behaviors.
The
promise_type
As we observed earlier, the return type
Task<T>
is the best entry-point for users to customize coroutine behaviors. C++ coroutine requires a
Task<T>::promise_type
type be defined.
the promise type can specify the coroutine behavior - most importantly when
add
is
call
ed, before
add
return
s, before the end of the coroutine’s lifetime (
destroy
)
the promise object (of the promise type) can be used to store additional state in the coroutine frame
When a coroutine is first
call
ed, C++ will automatically create a promise object for you, which lives inside the coroutine frame (that is allocated at the same time).
The Awaiter and the Awaitable
The
promise_type
covers the customization for
call
,
return
operation of a coroutine. We have
suspend
and
resume
left. Suspension takes place at well defined suspension points - initial_suspend(right after
call
), final_suspend(right before the end),
co_await
,
co_yield
. If one simply calls
add(1, 2)
with initial_suspend set to
suspend_always
, the coroutine is suspended. In most cases, one wants to customize the behavior of
suspend
so that the suspended coroutine can be
resume
d later. A coroutine can be suspended for two main reasons
to provide a customization opportunity - e.g.
initial_suspend
and
final_suspend
to wait for a dependency - a.k.a awaitable

4. **学习历史**：保存所有 corrections，方便复习和跟踪进度。
5. **免费使用**：无需注册或订阅。

该工具适合希望在日常交流中自然学习语言的用户。

data.author: znano
data.article_summary:
文章主要探讨了伊朗如何通过技术手段控制互联网，特别是在大规模抗议期间实施网络封锁。伊朗建立了国家信息网络（NIN），这是一个可以在切断国际互联网连接时维持国内服务运行的内部网络。NIN允许政府选择性关闭国际平台，同时保持本地服务运行，并通过伊朗防火墙（IRGFW）监控和过滤网络流量。

尽管封锁严密，但仍有漏洞。由于IP地址的动态分配和地理数据库的滞后，部分代理和VPN可能未被及时封锁。此外，工具如Pingtunnel可以通过ICMP协议传输数据，尽管速度慢但仍能提供连接。

此外，尽管伊朗严令禁止，一些伊朗人仍使用Starlink卫星网络绕过审查。Starlink终端通过NAT设置将流量路由至本地网络，使得伊朗ISP难以封锁此类连接。这些技术手段为民众在网络封锁期间提供了有限的通信渠道。

44551652.article_content:
A Technical Look at Iran’s Internet Shutdowns
At
13 Jul 2025
By
Zola Gonano
Every time mass protests erupt in Iran, a familiar pattern follows: the flow of information stops. The internet slows to a crawl or disappears entirely.
But how does a modern country survive cutting itself off from the internet? Wouldn’t that break everything?
Not quite, because the Islamic Republic has spent the last decade building an internet within the internet.
The National Information Network (NIN): Isolation by Design
Iran’s
National Information Network (NIN)
is a state-controlled intranet designed to keep domestic services running even when international connectivity is cut off. Think of it as a national sandbox: websites, banking portals, messaging apps, and e-government services that function entirely within Iran’s borders.
This setup serves two primary functions:
It
enables selective blackouts
: the state can block international platforms (like WhatsApp, Instagram, or news sites) while keeping local services (like state media, banking apps) fully operational.
It
forces ISPs to route traffic through government-controlled gateways
, making it easier to monitor, filter, or shut down parts of the network on demand.
Layered on top of this is the
IRGFW
—the Iranian Great Firewall. Modeled after China’s Great Firewall (GFW), but with stricter enforcement and more centralized control, it filters, blocks, and surveils traffic across the country.
On paper, it seems solid and impenetrable.
But there’s always a hole. Always.
What Can Be Done in This Situation?
The Iranian internet blockade is aggressive but it’s not perfect. Like any large-scale filtering system, it relies on outdated metadata, and static blocklists. And that’s where cracks begin to form.
The Known Flaw: IPs Are Rented, Not Owned
IPv4 addresses are limited and constantly reallocated. Most are rented and passed between hosting providers, resold between datacenters, or migrated across regions. The Iranian filtering system uses
GeoIP databases and BGP information
to decide which IP ranges to trust and which to block. But those records lag behind the changes.
An IP that once belonged to a local Iranian provider may now be assigned to a server in Amsterdam, but unless the IRGFW updates its filters in real time (which it doesn’t), that IP might still be allowed through.
This opens up a small but real opportunity:
scanning IP space
for reachable proxies, VPNs, or relays that haven’t yet been added to blocklists.
Yes, it’s mostly brute-force. But when everything else is down, even a single working IP can be a tunnel into the world.
Pingtunnel: Slow, but Better Than Nothing
To prevent scanning or circumvention, the IRGFW has tried to block most outbound protocols. But one thing they haven’t (yet) blocked completely is
ICMP
which is the protocol behind
ping
.
ICMP packets are typically used for diagnostics (checking whether a server is alive), and blocking them outright would break a lot of legitimate network functionality. So they’re still allowed, even under heavy shutdown conditions.
That’s where tools like
Pingtunnel
come in.
Pingtunnel allows you to
smuggle data inside ICMP packets
, essentially tunneling TCP traffic over a stream of pings. It’s really slow and It’s prone to packet loss. But it works, especially for text-based communication, command-line access, or sending small files.
It’s not secure against DPI or timing analysis. But in a shutdown scenario,
“slow but working” is better than nothing
. Even a shell session or basic messaging tool can be a critical line to the outside world.
Starlinks Behind NATs: Iranians Bypass Censorship Despite Criminalization
Despite Iran’s very aggressive criminalization of Starlink receivers, many Iranians still manage to get their hands on one of them. Starlink connections can be securely shared with others by routing traffic through NAT-enabled local routers using encrypted tunnels like WireGuard.
What Does “Behind NAT” Means?
Starlink provides an independent internet connection via satellite, bypassing local ISP infrastructure entirely. However, because Starlink devices receive
dynamic, often private IPv4/IPv6 addresses
and operate outside traditional ISP infrastructure, they are typically
behind NATs
when connected to local Iranian networks or user devices.
Here’s what this looks like:
A
Starlink terminal
(user terminal + router) connects to the satellite network and obtains an IP address from Starlink’s global network.
Meanwhile, the user’s devices in Iran are connected to the
local ISP’s network
, which uses its own IP addressing and NAT systems.
The user sets up a
local router or gateway inside Iran
that bridges these two networks, routing local traffic through the Starlink link.
How This Setup Bypasses Censorship
The key is that
Iranian ISPs and firewalls cannot effectively block Starlink traffic without physically confiscating or disabling the terminals
, because Starlink’s satellites communicate directly with user termina

data.title: Five companies now control over 90% of the restaurant food delivery market
data.author: goinggetthem
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：食品配送行业的市场集中与科技公司在其中的作用

不同观点：
• **市场集中是自然现象**：
   - 例如，[Aeolun]和[paxys]认为市场集中是商业的常态，90%以上的市场由少数几家公司控制是常见现象，不值得大惊小怪。
   - [Reason077]补充说，尽管两大公司控制大部分市场，但在具体区域内并未显著减少竞争，因为DoorDash和Deliveroo不在同一市场运营。

• **科技公司对社会的负面影响**：
   - [hn_throwaway_99]认为科技公司通过追求垄断对社会产生了负面影响，这种垄断趋势在互联网时代尤为明显，导致财富和权力的过度集中。

• **市场集中对消费者和从业者的影响**：
   - [NoPicklez]指出，市场集中是行业成熟的自然结果，全球市场的压力使得小公司难以生存。同时，澳大利亚对零工经济从业者权利的加强使得小公司难以承受成本。
   - [v5v3]提到，尽管大公司占据市场主导地位，但由于司机可以为多个公司工作，新进入者只要找到利基市场仍有机会。

• **独立配送和去中心化的可能性**：
   - [esco27]建议，餐饮行业可以通过开源平台实现去中心化，让餐厅自主管理菜单和订单，从而实现双赢。
   - [protocolture]则提出，为什么没有由配送司机拥有的公司来主导市场，认为这是有可能实现的。

• **消费者体验和市场反馈**：
   - [bravesoul2]批评食品配送服务体验不佳，如食物冷、送达时间不稳定、价格昂贵、营养价值低等。
   - [faizshah]提到一些餐厅通过自己的配送服务提供更便宜的选择，从而在价格上与大公司竞争。

补充讨论：
• **全球市场差异**：
   - [salomonk_mur]指出，Rappi在拉丁美洲是一个巨大的玩家，但在原文中未被提及，显示出不同地区市场的差异。

• **市场不确定性**：
   - [tptacek]认为，未来5年食品配送市场难以预测，因此当前的市场集中问题可能并不如看起来严重。

争议焦点：
• 市场集中是否对消费者和从业者不利，以及科技公司在其中的作用是好是坏。
• 去中心化和独立配送的可行性及其实际效果。

data.author: jxmorris12
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了如何通过强化学习（RL）将人工智能模型的计算能力扩展到10^26 FLOPs。作者提出，当前通过多环境并行扩展的方法复杂且混乱，建议使用RL在网络数据上进行下一token预测，从而从广泛的网络数据中学习推理能力，而不仅仅依赖数学和代码数据。文章还对比了预训练和RL两种扩展方式，指出预训练虽然有效，但其性能上限明显，而RL提供了一种不依赖模型大小或训练数据量的新扩展途径，可以在有限模型容量下生成更优答案。未来几年，AI研究将重点通过RL进行后训练扩展。

TLDR: Reinforcement learning (RL) is the next training technique for building frontier-level AI models. To make it better, we need to train on more data. The current approach of scaling many environments simultaneously is messy and complicated. Instead, I propose we find a way to do next-token prediction on the Web using RL. This way, we learn to reason from general web data, instead of just math and code.
I’ve spent a good part of the past year in denial.
Thanks for reading! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.
Subscribe
I was in denial because when
OpenAI released o1
, and explained their paradigm of
test-time compute
, I thought it was a good idea but mostly a way to get better performance out of models of fixed size. After all, letting models ‘think for longer’ by generating more tokens lets them do more internal computation.
The o1 release
from OpenAI was the first demonstration of a new type of language model, one that could think for longer to generate better answers.
So I wasn’t that surprised that these new models, termed
reasoning models
, gave better answers. And I especially wasn’t surprised when I found out these answers mostly came on problems that inherently require lots of computation, like difficult math and engineering test questions.
Don’t get me wrong: I always thought reasoning models were
interesting
. It’s cool to me that they generate “thinking traces” before giving answers (although the thinking traces might not be very reliable). And it’s amazing that the models were trained with reinforcement learning, a foundational technique in machine learning that was generally understood to be difficult to use effectively for real problems.
But I still thought of myself as a scale maximalist: all that really mattered, I thought, was training bigger models on more data. Anything else (read: reasoning models) appeared to be a coping mechanism, just a way to get by while we wait for the hardware needed to train bigger models.
I’ve spent the past few months working on RL research at Meta. It took a bit of time but I’ve come full-circle: something far more nuanced is happening with reasoning models. RL isn’t just a way to give models more compute.
RL training really is teaching models something
different
, a way to use compute to generate better answers
given finite model capacity. Through RL, models are clearly learning something that they’re not getting from pretraining.
Two waves of AI scaling
The AI research-into-production cycle moves through a few distinct phases. First, we as a community identify a new learning paradigm. Second, we find the correct datasets for training and design evaluations to know when our models are getting better, and by how much. And third, we scale it to all hell.
This cycle has happened already, exactly once. Pretraining. It started with the innocuous observation that models can learn quite a lot when trained on internet text data using next-token prediction. We realized that this gives intelligence improvements in just about every domain. And then we scaled.
We spent 2022–2024 scaling language model pretraining: first making models bigger, and now working to pack as much knowledge we could into models of various scales. We’ll spend the next several years scaling post-training using RL.
And to be clear, pretraining research is ongoing. We’re still figuring out how to scale our models via bigger datacenters and better hardware and more efficient algorithms. And we’re gathering more and better data every year. But the upper bound of pretraining performance is really clear. To build better models, we need to give them more parameters and train them on bigger datasets. This is what the AI labs have been working on for three years or so now.
But as the dust settles on the pretraining frenzy, reasoning models are showing us a new way to scale. We’ve found a way to make models better that’s independent of the number of training tokens or model size.
The murky path to RL scaling starts with
data
We’ve identified a new paradigm: learning to
reason
. But reasoning models are
in their GPT-3 era
: they’re trained on small datasets to do a narrow selection of tasks. We have a brittle proof-of-concept in the reasoning models of 2025. These models have achieved state-of-the-art scores on a small number of tasks, mostly expert-level math and coding questions.
In the case of pretraining, the path to progress was very clear. Models can learn via next-token prediction on just about
any
data, so we could simply scrape the entire Web and feed it to the models. And once we’d done that it became clear that our models were too small and we needed to make t

data.author: borski
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：餐厅通过社交媒体了解顾客偏好以提供个性化服务是否合适

不同观点：
• Ccecil引用电影《LA Story》中的场景，暗示这种做法早有预见，对文章标题的警示性提出质疑。
• prasadjoglekar认为尽管标题听起来不祥，但文章内容实际上是在描述餐厅如何通过细致的服务让顾客感到特别，并指出过去这类信息由家人提供，而现在可能由员工负责收集。
• Hnrobert42表示自己不希望在餐厅受到特别关注，认为这种做法让他感到不舒服，且需要假装兴奋是对他的一种负担。
• rglover将此做法与Danny Meyer的“收集信息”（collecting the dots）理念相比较，认为这是标准的高端 hospitality 做法，并指出文章标题有误导性。
• satvikpendem认为大多数普通顾客会喜欢这种个性化服务，并指出评论中的反对声音可能不代表主流顾客意见。
• astrange对SingleThread餐厅的经营方式提出批评，认为其模仿日本文化不准确，并指出真正的日本服务往往不迎合顾客特别要求。
• dceddia认为这些评论反映了人们如何被引导产生愤怒情绪，暗示对这种做法的过度反应。
• yapyap用讽刺口吻评论这种以付费服务替代真实亲密感的行为。
• userbinator认为只要信息是公开且获得顾客默许，餐厅的做法没有问题，但这种服务并非他所追求的体验。
• smitelli表示自己不喜欢受到过多的个人关注，这种服务让他感到不适。
• alganet认为基于数字内容的过滤将成为趋势，但这种做法最终可能因数据质量问题而失败。
• steveBK123将此做法比作私有化的社会信用评分，暗示其潜在的负面影响。
• joenot443对餐厅的创意和真诚的 hospitality 表示赞赏，认为一些评论者过度担忧，并认为这种做法本质上是善意且积极的。
• asdf6969用讽刺语气建议通过拍摄店主孩子的照片来建立更好的业务关系。
• jqpabc123认为这种做法可能开启一个反乌托邦的噩梦，主张餐厅应专注于提高食物和服务的质量，而非侵犯隐私和迎合虚荣。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于隐私问题和个性化服务的平衡。一部分人认为这是高端 hospitality 的表现，另一部分人则担忧隐私侵犯和不必要的关注。
• 部分评论者对餐厅模仿其他文化的准确性提出质疑，并指出真正的高端服务不应依赖过度收集顾客信息。
• 评论中还涉及到对这种做法的过度情绪反应以及对社会趋势的批评，如私有化的社会信用评分。
• 总体来看，讨论反映了人们对个性化服务与隐私权之间的复杂权衡，以及对现代技术在服务行业应用的忧虑。

data.title: Hungary's oldest library fighting to save 100k books from a beetle infestation
data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: 匈牙利潘诺恩哈尔姆修道院的图书馆正面临药材甲虫侵扰，导致约10万本古老手装书受到影响。这些书将被放入密封塑料袋中，在无氧环境下用纯氮处理六周以消灭甲虫。潘诺恩哈尔姆修道院建于996年，拥有40万册藏书，其中包括13世纪完整的圣经手抄本和数百本印刷术发明前的古 manuscripts。尽管最古老和珍贵的书籍未受影响，但任何损坏都被视为对文化和历史遗产的打击。气候变化可能促使了甲虫的繁殖，因为气温升高加速了它们的生长周期。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何保护潘诺恩哈尔马修道院的古老书籍及其面临的问题，包括气候变化、害虫侵扰以及技术和资源限制。

• GCA10认为修道院的图书馆尽管建筑美观，但对于现代学者而言，其收藏的古籍更多是好奇之物，而非重要的学术资源。他指出，由于地处农村，缺乏周边研究社区和城市资源，因此没有空调等现代设施。此外，他表示，从学术影响力来看，这个图书馆并非世界上最有价值的收藏之一。

• joecool1029对原始新闻来源提供了链接，并指出甲虫侵扰是一种常见害虫问题，而非罕见现象。他批评了某些评论的不实信息，并提供了关于甲虫种类的参考资料。

• johnisgood从个人经历出发，讨论了气候变化对匈牙利的影响，特别是气温升高导致冬季无雪、夏季酷热的现象。他还提到由于基础设施问题，许多公寓无法安装空调，这使得炎热的夏季更加难熬。

• mensetmanusman提出了使用医疗设备中的伽马辐射传送带对书籍进行杀虫处理的技术解决方案，并建议了布达佩斯和德国的具体设施。

• dr_dshiv关注未被扫描或翻译的古籍，建议建立一个中央系统来追踪这些书籍，以展示未完成的工作，并猜测大部分新拉丁作品尚未被扫描和翻译。

• 讨论中涉及了气候变化对当地环境的实际影响，如johnisgood提到的季节变化和气温升高问题。
• 提出了多种技术解决方案，如书籍的伽马辐射杀虫法，显示了对保护文化遗产的创新思考。
• 对修道院缺乏现代设施如空调的问题进行了探讨，涉及技术和经济可行性。

争议焦点：
• 对修道院图书馆的学术价值存在不同看法，GCA10认为其主要为 curiosities，而其他评论者并未直接反驳但关注其文化和历史价值。

44552362.article_content:
A restorer shows an old book with holes in its pages due to a drugstore beetle infestation, at the Pannonhalma Archabbey's library in Pannonhalma, Hungary, on July 3.
Pannonhalma Archabbey via AP file
July 13, 2025, 1:18 PM EDT
/
Source
:
The Associated Press
By
The Associated Press
PANNONHALMA, Hungary — Tens of thousands of centuries-old books are being pulled from the shelves of a medieval abbey in Hungary in an effort to save them from a beetle infestation that could wipe out centuries of history.
The 1,000-year-old Pannonhalma Archabbey is a sprawling Benedictine monastery that is one of Hungary's oldest centers of learning and a UNESCO World Heritage site.
Restoration workers are removing about 100,000 handbound books from their shelves and carefully placing them in crates, the start of a disinfection process that aims to kill the tiny beetles burrowed into them.
The drugstore beetle, also known as the bread beetle, is often found among dried foodstuffs like grains, flour and spices. But they also are attracted to the gelatin and starch-based adhesives found in books.
They have been found in a section of the library housing around a quarter of the abbey's 400,000 volumes.
"This is an advanced insect infestation which has been detected in several parts of the library, so the entire collection is classified as infected and must be treated all at the same time," said Zsófia Edit Hajdu, the chief restorer on the project. "We've never encountered such a degree of infection before."
Abbey houses historical treasures
The beetle invasion was first detected during a routine library cleaning. Employees noticed unusual layers of dust on the shelves and then saw that holes had been burrowed into some of the book spines. Upon opening the volumes, burrow holes could be seen in the paper where the beetles chewed through.
Books are kept in hermetically sealed plastic sacks for disinfection, at the Pannonhalma Archabbey's library in Pannonhalma, Hungary, on July 3.
Bela Szandelszky / AP file
The abbey at Pannonhalma was founded in 996, four years before the establishment of the Kingdom of Hungary. Sitting upon a tall hill in northwestern Hungary, the abbey houses the country's oldest collection of books, as well as many of its earliest and most important written records.
For over 1,000 years, the abbey has been among the most prominent religious and cultural sites in Hungary and all of Central Europe, surviving centuries of wars and foreign incursions such as the Ottoman invasion and occupation of Hungary in the 16th century.
Ilona Ásványi, director of the Pannonhalma Archabbey library, said she is "humbled" by the historical and cultural treasures the collection holds whenever she enters.
"It is dizzying to think that there was a library here a thousand years ago, and that we are the keepers of the first book catalogue in Hungary," she said.
Among the library's most outstanding works are 19 codices, including a complete Bible from the 13th century. It also houses several hundred manuscripts predating the invention of the printing press in the mid-15th century and tens of thousands of books from the 16th century.
While the oldest and rarest prints and books are stored separately and have not been infected, Ásványi said any damage to the collection represents a blow to cultural, historical and religious heritage.
"When I see a book chewed up by a beetle or infected in any other way, I feel that no matter how many copies are published and how replaceable the book is, a piece of culture has been lost," she said.
Books will spend weeks in an oxygen-free environment
To kill the beetles, the crates of books are being placed into tall, hermetically sealed plastic sacks from which all oxygen is removed. After six weeks in the pure nitrogen environment, the abbey hopes all the beetles will be destroyed.
Before being reshelved, each book will be individually inspected and vacuumed. Any book damaged by the pests will be set aside for later restoration work.
Climate change may have contributed
The abbey, which hopes to reopen the library at the beginning of next year, believes the effects of climate change played a role in spurring the beetle infestation as average temperatures rise rapidly in Hungary.
A priest wearing a face mask stands by books kept in hermetically sealed plastic sacks for disinfection at the Pannonhalma Archabbey's library in Pannonhalma, Hungary, on July 3.
Bela Szandelszky / AP file
Hajdu, the chief restorer, said higher temperatures have allowed the beetles to undergo several more development cycles annually than they could in cooler weather.

44552362.article_summary: 匈牙利潘诺恩哈尔姆修道院的图书馆正面临药材甲虫侵扰，导致约10万本古老手装书受到影响。这些书将被放入密封塑料袋中，在无氧环境下用纯氮处理六周以消灭甲虫。潘诺恩哈尔姆修道院建于996年，拥有40万册藏书，其中包括13世纪完整的圣经手抄本和数百本印刷术发明前的古 manuscripts。尽管最古老和珍贵的书籍未受影响，但任何损坏都被视为对文化和历史遗产的打击。气候变化可能促使了甲虫的繁殖，因为气温升高加速了它们的生长周期。
