• 争议焦点之一是品牌提供的过多型号选择和配置问题，使得消费者难以找到理想产品。
• 另一个讨论点是MacBook的长期满意度与其他品牌的对比，特别是硬件质量和软件体验。
• Linux和Windows系统的硬件兼容性也是讨论的一个重要方面，尤其是对GPU和端口支持的需求。
• 对基本功能和性价比的关注反映了一些用户对实用性的偏好，而不是追求最高端的配置。

44558112.article_content:
Nate
Linux Hardware
July 13, 2025
6 Minutes
This is a bit of a rant; feel free to skip it if you’re here for the KDE content.
This isn’t the first time I’ve blogged about the dearth of truly great PC laptops out there, and I suspect it won’t be the last.
I limit myself to a single computer for simplicity’s sake, so it has to be a laptop. And since I replaced my
2020 Lenovo ThinkPad X1 Yoga
a year ago, I haven’t succeeded at finding a truly great replacement yet. From a certain point of view, you could say I’m a picky buyer, judging by my
list of requirements
. But frankly, I think these requirements are not that unreasonable. All I want is a laptop that gets the basics right:
Good screen with a DPI suitable for 175-200% scaling, generally between 240 and 280 DPI
Good keyboard with text navigation keys (Home, End, Page Up, and Page Down) and a sensible layout: delete at the top right, no stupid replacement of normal modifier keys with fingerprint readers or copilot keys, no tiny arrow keys, etc.
Good touchpad that’s precise, doesn’t lag, and allows clicking on most or all of the total area
Good speakers that get reasonably loud and don’t have downward-facing tweeters
8 hours of battery life with low usage
Reasonably fast CPU
Reasonable GPU performance for desktop compositing and playing couple-year-old games
Replaceable disk
Just the basics; no great world-shattering innovation needed, and that’s before I narrow the search to laptops that lack NVIDIA GPUs and have touch or 2-in-1 capabilities (which I quite like and are highly useful for testing touch support in KDE software). So it has to have great Linux and Plasma compatibility too!
I’ve closely followed the PC laptop market for 9 years, maintaining a giant spreadsheet of every laptop model and how they fare on the above characteristics plus many more:
The multi-year trend is “one step forward, one step back.” Most companies still change their laptops’ keyboard layouts in random negative ways every year; ship with stupid screen resolutions, woefully bad speakers, and disappointing touchpads; and stuff the most powerful processor and GPU in there and don’t focus enough on tuning the cooling, power usage, and fan profiles.
Some examples from my own usage:
My 2016 HP Spectre x360 was slow and had a poor screen DPI and a laggy touchpad. The 2024 model fixed those problems but lost its HDMI ports and text nav keys, and the USB-A port has a fiddly and annoying little hinge that’s hard to use and will eventually break. And then the 14″ version was canceled in 2025.
My 2020 Lenovo ThinkPad X1 Yoga was also slow, had miserable battery life and a loud fan, put the Fn and PrintScreen keys in inconvenient places, and its high resolution 4K screen option had
too
high a DPI, wasting energy. The 2025 model fixed those issues but lost the excellent quad speaker system, garaged pen, and the third key to the right of the spacebar that let you re-bind one of them into being a second Meta key.
None of this would be a problem if you could customize and upgrade laptops like you can with desktops, but you can’t. Even on the
Framework 13 laptop
which makes this an explicit selling point and has made huge leaps in 4 years, there still aren’t aftermarket speaker modules that sound good or a keyboard deck with text nav keys. And the touch/2-in-1 capabilities are only offered on the 12″ model.
Where are the great laptops?
Let’s step back a bit and try to figure out what’s going on here. We have an industry of over a dozen PC manufacturers selling thousands of products, but few truly great ones that are satisfactory in
all
ways, not just a few.
I feel that a major problem is over-complicated product lines. Let’s look at what the big companies offer.
Here’s
Lenovo
:
Seven product lines (or is it eight; there’s an extra one in the sidebar not shown in the main view) and 330 distinct models! How can a normal person who isn’t a laptop enthusiast find anything in here? Even my eyes glaze over when I’m trying to distinguish the differences between the models and product lines.
HP further complicates things by having separate sites for consumer laptops and business laptops. First the
consumer
laptops:
12 product lines with 67 models. Already a lot. But now add in the
business laptops
:
7 product lines with 352 models! Absurd. HP implicitly acknowledges the problem by advertising a sales advisor you can chat with to help you make heads or tails of this overwhelming mess (and maybe steer you towards more expensive models):
In total, HP offers
19 product lines and 419 models
. Madness, I tell you. Sheer madness.
ASUS makes it even harder by dividing their models into micro-targeted audiences, which makes no sense since there’s overlap in all these use cases and only limited differences between what any of them need in a laptop:
Ultimately I found 8 product lines with 289 models on the US site. Yikes!
MSI does similar segmentation but finds a way to make it even worse by putting more models in

data.title: It's so on. Trump declares war on podcast bros over Epstein
data.author: myrtlehinch
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论特朗普对杰弗里·爱泼斯坦事件相关讨论的强硬态度，特别是针对播客主持人对此事的持续关注。特朗普在回应记者提问时显得不耐烦，质疑为何人们还在谈论爱泼斯坦。文章指出，尽管官方声称联邦调查局和司法部结束了对爱泼斯坦的调查，但许多疑点仍未解开，包括爱泼斯坦的“黑皮书”下落、吉斯莱恩·麦克斯韦的证词内容以及一些高调人物与爱泼斯坦的关系等。文章暗示可能存在高层掩盖，并提到特朗普曾表示愿意公布爱泼斯坦的文件，但现在似乎改变了立场，可能迫于压力。整体而言，文章质疑官方对爱泼斯坦案的处理透明度，并怀疑背后有更深层的政治操作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于深层政府（deep state）及相关阴谋论的可信性和具体表现

不同观点：
• [Havoc的观点]  
  - 认为首次听到关于深层政府的描述是可信的，暗示存在一个真正的幕后操控力量。  
  - 例子：提到深层政府的概念，似乎指向一个隐藏的权力操控实体。

• [NicoJuicy的观点]  
  - 对几件事情表示猜测：  
    1. 认为爱泼斯坦的名单由特朗普及其同伙掌控，以用于对其他共和党人的勒索。  
    2. 猜测某些播客受到俄罗斯资助，且特朗普与俄罗斯关系破裂，因此这些播客现在反对特朗普。  
    3. 质疑特朗普及其团队中是否存在被普京安插的代理人，并暗示特朗普可能会"突然坠窗身亡"。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点  
  - 关于深层政府的真实性和具体表现形式存在争议。Havoc认为某种形式的深层政府是可信的，而NicoJuicy则将焦点放在特朗普、俄罗斯和共和党内部的潜在黑幕交易及可能的阴谋。

The official rationale for closing the FBI investigation into Jeffrey Epstein stinks and President Trump must know it - even if he can manage to feign incredulity that anyone should still want to talk about the disgraced financier.
‘‘Are you still talking about Jeffrey Epstein? This guy’s been talked about for years,’ he responded testily on Tuesday to a reporter’s question at a cabinet meeting about whether Epstein had ever been an intelligence agency asset.
‘Are people still talking about this guy? This creep? That is unbelievable. Do you want to waste the time? I mean I can’t believe you’re asking a question on Epstein.’
Crucially, Trump didn’t deny Epstein was a spook, and neither did Attorney General Pam Bondi to whom he passed the question. “I have no knowledge about that. We can get back to you about that,” she obfuscated.
What an insane place the Epstein saga has now arrived at, a place in which - according to the official statement released late on Monday - we are now required by the FBI and the Department of Justice to believe Epstein did not traffic ‘over one thousand’ young women to powerful men as part of an industrial-scale honey trap blackmail operation, but rather that he molested them himself, in private.
As for all the entertaining he did on his Little Saint James island, or at his various multimillion dollar properties – where guests included Bill Gates, Bill Clinton and Prince Andrew – hell, he must have just really loved parties.
Stating that there seems obviously to be a high level, deep state cover-up taking place on all things Epstein-related can no longer be dismissed simply as a nut-job conspiracy theory, no matter how much those involved might like to. Why not? Well, because so many of the people now asking us to believe the unbelievable not so long ago themselves called bullshit.
In 2023, current head of the FBI Kash Patel was asked by podcast host Glenn Beck who he believed had possession of Epstein’s black book of clients.
He said: “FBI. That’s under direct control of the director of the FBI… This is another government gangster operation. All these local law enforcement communities get funding from the DOJ and FBI for local programs. If you don’t cooperate, you’re not getting your million dollars for this, and that’s a lot of money to these local districts. That’s how they play the game. That’s why you don’t have the black book.”
In 2021, Vice President JD Vance responded to allegations Epstein’s close associate Ghislaine Maxwell’s lawyers had made a deal with the DOJ to ensure her black book of contacts would never see the light of day, by stating: “What possible interest would the US government have in keeping Epstein’s clients secret?... If you’re a journalist and you’re not asking questions about this case you should be ashamed of yourself. What purpose do you even serve?”
Exactly.
There is so much about the Epstein case that is deeply suspect. receive
a thirteen-month work release deal rather than a maximum 45-year jail sentence for the crime of raping girls as young as 14?
Also, was the $158 million dollars paid to Epstein between 2012 and 2017 by Apollo Global Management Services CEO Leon Black really only for ‘estate planning, tax and philanthropic advice,’ as claimed? It seems a tremendous amount. Interestingly, Black was twice on the receiving end of lawsuits alleging he raped young women at properties owned by Epstein. He has denied all accusations.
Then, of course, there is all the other strange stuff: the cameras filming the door to the cell in which Epstein supposedly committed suicide being on the
blink
. The guards responsible for supervising him being
asleep
. Epstein’s friend the modelling agent Jean-Luc Brunel - who like him supposedly committed suicide in a Paris jail while awaiting trial for human trafficking - being
pictured
on Little Saint James island wearing a cap bearing the words ‘Israel Army’.

data.article_summary:
Loris Cro的文章介绍了Zig编程语言即将推出的新异步I/O设计及其与async/await复兴的关系。新设计引入了一个`Io`接口，由调用者提供，允许开发者选择具体的I/O实现并注入到代码中。这一改变使得代码能够更好地参与事件循环，处理阻塞/非阻塞I/O，并有机会实现并行操作。

文章通过示例展示了如何使用新接口。第一个示例没有表达并发，因此不能利用并行性。第二个示例通过`async`和`await`实现并发，可以在事件驱动I/O中更好地运行，同时也兼容阻塞I/O。

此外，文章还提到在处理`Future`时需要注意错误管理，避免未能正确`await`导致的资源泄漏，并介绍了如何通过取消任务来正确释放资源。这种新设计让开发者可以更灵活地控制I/O和并发操作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Zig语言中函数着色问题是否被解决以及IO系统的设计和实现

不同观点：
• dminik认为Zig并没有完全解决函数着色问题。他指出，尽管Zig消除了async/sync的区别，但IO和非IO函数之间的区别依然存在，且需要提供IO作为参数。他还强调函数调用仍然依赖于上下文，而Zig并没有真正解决这个问题。尽管如此，他认为Zig在抽象实现方面做得很好，比Rust更成功。
• hardwaresofton提到类似的概念在Rust中已经被讨论过，并提供了一些参考链接，暗示Zig的IO设计并非全新的创新。
• do_not_redeem对Zig采用绿色线程（fibers）表示担忧，认为这是过时的技术，可能导致性能问题，并提到Rust在1.0之前就因为性能问题移除了类似的特性。
• garaetjjte对Zig声称解决函数着色问题表示怀疑，认为Zig的IO实现仍然是基于阻塞方法，而这些方法在其他语言中也能实现。他提出两种可能的解决方案：让每个函数都是async，或编译每个函数两次以选择合适的调用方式。
• henrikl认为Zig在标准IO操作中引入运行时多态性是不必要的，因为大多数情况下IO实现可以在编译时确定。
• eestrada支持Zig的IO参数设计，认为它允许多种实现且避免用户关心具体实现，符合Zig的“不为不用的东西付费”的理念。
• sevensor强调io.async表达的是异步性，而不是并发性，认为这种分离是非常聪明的设计。
• Cloudef喜欢IO接口，因为它可以创建语言级别的虚拟文件系统。
• n42对Zig的IO设计感到兴奋，特别提到了对WebAssembly的潜在影响。
• rastignack通过实践（编写简单的ssh服务器）发现新的IO设计使事件循环和IO更容易理解。
• wucke13认为Zig的IO设计类似于代数效应系统，IO传递类似于效应处理器。
• nextaccountic关注定时器和io.sleep的问题，并询问是否使用了io_uring。
• noelwelsh质疑Zig团队是否承认他们正在走一条已有的路径，暗示他们可能没有提到借鉴了其他语言的实现。
• xmorse建议实现“上下文”机制，以避免在每个函数中添加IO参数。
• anonymoushn认为新的设计是倒退，他更喜欢编译时泛型，而不是运行时通过vtable访问的系统。

补充讨论：
• 函数着色问题的核心在于上下文依赖，Zig是否真正解决这个问题存在争议。
• 对Zig采用绿色线程的性能担忧和与其他语言（如Rust）的比较。
• 对Zig的IO设计是否必要及其对WebAssembly和系统编程的潜在影响。
• 关于如何在Zig中实现异步和并发操作的具体技术讨论，如代数效应系统和上下文传递机制。

• n42对Zig的IO设计感到兴奋，特别提到了对WebAssembly的潜在影响。
• rastignack通过实践（编写简单的ssh服务器）发现新的IO设计使事件循环和IO更容易理解。
• wucke13认为Zig的IO设计类似于代数效应系统，IO传递类似于效应处理器。
• nextaccountic关注定时器和io.sleep的问题，并询问是否使用了io_uring。
• noelwelsh质疑Zig团队是否承认他们正在走一条已有的路径，暗示他们可能没有提到借鉴了其他语言的实现。
• xmorse建议实现“上下文”机制，以避免在每个函数中添加IO参数。
• anonymoushn认为新的设计是倒退，他更喜欢编译时泛型，而不是运行时通过vtable访问的系统。

补充讨论：
• 函数着色问题的核心在于上下文依赖，Zig是否真正解决这个问题存在争议。
• 对Zig采用绿色线程的性能担忧和与其他语言（如Rust）的比较。
• 对Zig的IO设计是否必要及其对WebAssembly和系统编程的潜在影响。
• 关于如何在Zig中实现异步和并发操作的具体技术讨论，如代数效应系统和上下文传递机制。

data.title: Let me pay for Firefox
data.author: csmantle
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Mozilla基金会及其产品（尤其是Firefox浏览器）的资金使用、产品开发方向以及是否应向Mozilla捐款或付费

不同观点：
• 一些用户（如gr4vityWall和lenkite）对Mozilla的资金使用感到失望，认为捐款可能被用于无关紧要的项目或高管奖金，而不是用于提升浏览器性能。他们更愿意支持像Floorp这样的浏览器 fork，因为这些项目更专注于改进技术。
• mzhaase认为当前依赖广告的资金模式赋予广告商过多权力，主张更多付费产品以减少广告对社会的影响。
• DoctorOW为Mozilla辩护，指出Mozilla已经简化了项目，专注于浏览器及相关工具，并提到前CEO已经离职，质疑批评者的真正诉求。
• jurgenaut23提出语言的歧义（“免费” vs “自由”）可能影响开源软件的发展，并以法语为例，说明为“libre”软件付费并不矛盾。
• cuillevel3分享了个人经历，对Mozilla取消Pocket Premium及相关数据处理不当表示不满，表示不会再次购买其产品。
• int0x29强调Mozilla在安全工作和浏览器维护中的重要性，认为批评者没有意识到维持这些工作的成本，并警告若Mozilla倒下，其他fork项目也难以存活。
• freediver和bradfa支持为Firefox付费的模式，认为这样可以更好地对齐用户和开发者的利益，并提出类似Bitwarden的收费模式作为参考。
• McDyver推荐Ladybird浏览器作为Mozilla的替代方案，认为其值得更多财务支持。
• countWSS以讽刺口吻提出如何让Firefox市场份额降至0%的策略，批评Mozilla在用户体验和功能上的不足。
• beloch以WinRAR为例，建议Firefox可以尝试类似“试用软件”的模式，不强制收费但通过礼貌提醒获取自愿付费。
• greatgib批评Mozilla高管的贪婪和浪费，认为应更有效地使用资金提升Firefox，并指出Thunderbird等项目因缺乏资金未达预期。
• captainepoch认为Mozilla已经有足够资金用于Firefox开发，只需将部分资金重新分配给工程师团队即可改进浏览器。
• Imustaskforhelp表示支持像librewolf和Ladybird这样的项目，认为它们更值得资助，但对Mozilla的资金使用持怀疑态度。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于Mozilla的资金使用是否合理及其产品开发方向是否符合用户期望。
• 部分用户对Mozilla高管的薪酬和项目的取消表示不满，认为资金被浪费在无关项目上。
• 一些用户支持为浏览器付费的模式，认为这样可以更好地支持开发并提升产品质量。
• 对于浏览器fork项目（如Floorp和Ladybird）的支持和期望，部分用户认为这些项目更值得资助。
• 语言和文化的差异（如“gratuit” vs “libre”）在讨论开源软件付费问题时也被提及，影响了用户的看法。

data.title: Switching to Claude Code and VSCode Inside Docker
data.author: timsh
data.article_summary: 本文主要介绍了作者从原先的AI编码设置（使用ChatGPT Plus和Cursor Pro）转向使用Claude Code in Docker的经历，并提供了一个简要的操作指南。作者提到原先设置存在两个主要问题：响应速度慢和AI代理安全风险。为解决这些问题，作者选择了Claude的20美元订阅服务，并通过Docker容器限制其访问权限，以提高安全性和响应速度。最终，作者在VSCode的"Dev Container"功能中运行Claude Code，达到了预期的效果。文中还提供了一个GitHub链接，供读者查看具体操作和代码。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开发环境中的容器化工具使用，尤其是针对VSCode、Claude Code、Docker等工具的讨论。

不同观点：
• CGamesPlay认为，即使不喜欢VSCode，也可以通过使用微软开发的devcontainer CLI工具实现类似功能，虽然需要手动处理一些如端口转发的问题，但通过额外工具可以解决。他还提到自己开发了一个工具来处理端口转发。
• mkagenius更偏向于使用Apple的内置容器技术，认为其速度快，并且与Claude Code、Gemini CLI等工具集成良好。他开源了自己开发的工具CodeRunner，但指出该工具只适用于M1/M2/M3/M4芯片的Mac。
• sothatsit强调容器的优势在于可以轻松启动和丢弃代理，而无需担心成本或安全性问题。他还提到即使出现问题，Git也能轻松还原更改。
• photonthug主张更多地采用容器化开发方式，认为这样可以解决很多关于工具和过程的可重复性问题，并减少系统中不必要的依赖。
• kaffekaka担心Claude Code的安全性，提出使用单独的用户账户是否能解决这个问题，但不确定是否足够。
• intellectronica提到Claude Code的开放替代品，认为可以选择其他模型和经济方案。
• crawshaw指出容器化开发可以让代理并行运行，并允许它们执行一些在本地桌面上不希望执行的操作，如安装工具或调试。
• scosman偏好使用chatGPT codex而非Claude Code，因为前者可以在各自的云容器中运行，减少了暴露秘密或破坏环境的风险。
• hintymad质疑使用Docker进行开发的必要性，认为配置开发容器可能是一种麻烦。
• tkiolp4认为在容器或虚拟机中开发是更常见的做法，因为不信任在自己的机器上运行npm、pip等工具。
• tosh指出在macOS上使用devcontainer的一些优缺点，如减少CLI工具调用失败和等待时间，但在通知和工具集成方面存在一些不便。
• arscan提到GitHub CodeSpaces的兼容性，认为这是一个非常好的开发体验，尤其是在Chromebook等设备上。
• abrookewood提到像phoenix.new这样的服务，认为其核心思想就是让AI代理拥有对环境的完全控制，而不影响本地机器。
• ed_mercer不理解为何大家对Claude Code的安全性有如此多的担忧，认为只要合理使用，就不会出现问题。
• tartakovsky提出两个问题：对Claude Code的安全性担忧是否合理，以及为什么AI代码生成提供商不提供容器化服务。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Claude Code等AI工具的安全性和容器化开发的必要性。部分开发者认为容器化提供了更好的隔离和安全性，而另一些开发者则认为只要合理配置和使用，不使用容器也不会带来太大问题。
• 讨论中还涉及到不同的开发工具和环境，如VSCode、Apple的内置容器技术、GitHub CodeSpaces等，开发者们根据自己的需求和偏好选择不同的工具和方案。
• 一些开发者关注容器化开发的便利性和可重复性，认为容器化可以减少开发环境中的摩擦，并提高工作效率。

44533044.article_content:
Last night I finished a transition from my old AI coding setup I've been using for a while to running Claude Code in Docker using VSCode's "Dev Container" feature.
In this post I lay out a few of my thoughts on why I wanted to switch to something in the first place, and also a short guide for those who want to do the same.
If you are here just for the guide + code (a tiny single file), here it is:
https://github.com/tim-sha256/claude-in-docker
🥺
Important note!
I'm not a professional vibecoder (thanks god) and I don't generate AI code on 9-5 basis (meh)
I'm just a casual user occasionally getting help from llms on my projects, all of them being not corporate-serious-guys-enterprise-grade.
I'm not looking for the most advanced 100x dev tools or workflows, nor $100+ subscriptions whose token limits I'll probably only reach once a year on a sleepless night.
Before and why
Until yesterday I've been using such setup:
ChatGPT Plus 20$ subscription for occasional chats mostly unrelated to code, except for quickies and desperate attempts to feed o3 a bunch of code that Claude can't crack and get it all solved (mostly unsuccessful).
Cursor Pro for additional 20$ (or how do they call it these days?) - for all "serious" coding.
Which works all right, is convenient (been stuck with Cursor since August '24 and GPT since '23 without actively seeking an alternative), but has a couple issues that started to bug me recently.
Issue 1: I'm greedy and I want my responses fast
Before Cursor went into drain-users stage recently, I did not use up all 500 requests / month not a single time while working on 1-2 projects during my free time (approx. 40-60 hours a month).
Maybe I could've paid less on token-based plan, but I didn't really care – $20 is $20 :)
But after their update removing the 500 requests limit "so you can enjoy unlimited requests to almost any model", I've been extremely upset by Cursor due to their inadequate rate limits.
Sometimes I would type a prompt for Sonnet 4 (not even Opus...) and wait for 2-5 minutes for anything to happen, which is a complaint I've seen quite a lot in Cursor-related chats and on Reddit.
There is an option to switch back to a proprietary and seemingly not as profitable 500 requests pricing mode, but I don't think it'll last much longer.  Or use the free version and go out for a smoke break after every request.
Which led me to think about my spending and the satisfaction I get in return: is it still worth 40$ or is there a better way?
Well, for now I've settled with Claude 20$ subscription and consider it a better fit for my use case for a couple of reasons:
$20 is less than 40$
I still get to send a pic of a shelf with various cleaning products to some chat app on my phone and ask "Which of these do I need to do X?", which works surprisingly well almost all the time
I have a similar-or-even-better web chat experience to work on stuff unrelated to code
Finally, and most importantly – I get Claude Code with:
reasonable limits
clear token spending indication
everybody constantly says Claude Code rocks, right?
I like cli stuff in general
vs code integration makes the IDE experience essentially the same (or even a bit better)
Ok, looks like I'm settled for now, end of story. Or what else?
Issue 2: I'm trying to be realistic about AI Agent security
Simply put: I believe running an AI Agent that has access to your entire file system, terminal and secrets is dangerous and will eventually lead to some problems.
Think of it as if you gave access to your computer to a cheap overseas freelance dev who you don't really know and can only chat with. How does that sound?
I stumble upon llm security-related stuff every day and occasionally read some of it. And generally, the situation is not getting better.
For instance, I've seen around 10 posts about very serious vulnerabilities in MCPs like
this one,
a few sad stories where cursor decided to delete something useful like all Ableton projects using
rm -rf
, and even threads saying that Claude
learned to bypass Cursor built-in command blacklist
in Yolo mode.
Basically, you have a choice: either accept each single command manually (which I think is a reasonable approach but I'm too lazy) or trust the above mentioned freelancer with everything you have and hope that some barriers will stop it and nothing bad will happen.
Or are there any other options?
Now and why
Ok, so I want to use Claude Code, but at the same time want to restrict it somehow so it can't fuck up my entire computer.
First idea which came to me turned to be the one that I'd go with (who could've thought): put that thing into a box with nothing but the project(s) in it, give it the least possible access and close the box.
In other words, launch Claude Code in Docker and work on the project inside the container.
What you get from that:
Claude can only access files from inside the container or in the provided volumes, mounted or not
It also most certainly can't break anything outside the con

data.title: A software conference that advocates for quality
data.author: leoncaet
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了将于7月12日至14日在瑞典举办的一场活动，活动将通过Twitch直播。每日有不同主题的演讲，涵盖编程历史、物理引擎并行化、软件开发工具、游戏车辆编程、实时调试器可视化架构、音频技术、渲染技术、深度学习与计算机视觉以及编译器设计等内容。物理参与为邀请制，不公开发售门票。线上可免费观看直播和录播。活动地点在一个迷人的小镇。更多信息可通过订阅时事通讯或通过Twitter咨询组织者Sam、Sander和Charlie。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对某软件质量会议的评论和争议

不同观点：
• **对会议效果的怀疑**：
  - [burnt-resistor] 认为会议和书籍承诺的“这次会有所不同”往往是空谈，实际效果有限。过程、工具和 diligence 看似是明显的路径，但质疑 AI 介入可能带来的经验不足问题。

data.title: Strategies for Fast Lexers
data.author: xnacly
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了作者在开发名为"purple garden"的基于S-expr的语言时，如何优化词法分析器（Lexer）以提高其速度。"purple garden"语言注重性能，词法分析器是编译过程中的初始阶段，负责将字符流转换为有意义的词法单元（tokens），供解析器生成抽象语法树（AST），最终由编译器生成字节码并由虚拟机执行。

文章详细讲解了词法单元的定义，包含类型、起始位置、长度和行号等信息，并展示了如何用C语言实现一个简洁高效的词法分析器。作者通过状态迭代字符，匹配关键字、数字和符号等，同时介绍了一些优化策略，如使用计算goto（computed gotos）来提高词法分析的速度。

文章最后提供了基准测试结果以验证其性能优化方法的有效性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： lexer 优化的多种方法及其性能影响

不同观点：
• **使用 `musttail` 属性替代 computed gotos**：sparkie 建议使用 `musttail` 属性来替代 computed gotos，以确保在不同编译器下都能优化，并具有更好的模块化特性。这种方法要求函数签名一致，但可以避免 computed goto 在某些编译器上不被支持的问题。
• **使用 `FILE*` 操作流式数据**：thechao 偏好于让 lexer 操作 `FILE*` 而不是 string-view，以便处理流式数据。尽管这可能带来性能损耗，但增加了操作的灵活性。同时，thechao 提出通过减少 lexer 中的决策逻辑来提高性能，并提到如果关键词长度较短，可以直接使用 `uint64_t` 进行快速比较。
• **完美哈希函数用于关键词比较**：kklisura 提到使用完美哈希函数来加速关键词的比较，这种方法在 PostgreSQL 中被使用，并提供了相关参考链接。
• **SIMD 加速字符匹配**：zX41ZdbW 推荐参考 ClickHouse 的 SQL Lexer，它通过支持 SIMD 和避免内存分配来实现加速。o11c 也提到使用 SIMD 或 SWAR 技术来跳过尽可能多的字符，从而提高性能。
• **手写词法分析器的高性能实现**：adev_ 分享了自己为 Swift 衍生语言实现的词法分析器，使用 C++ 和显式的 SIMD 向量化，不依赖宏和汇编，同时通过编译时生成查找表来保持代码小巧和可维护。

补充讨论：
• **`strcspn` 与 `strspn` 的使用**：o11c 指出使用 `strcspn` 可以加速字符串处理，但其性能受限于实现，并且对于较大的字符集需要使用 `strspn`。
• **跳表与 `switch` 的性能比较**：psanchez 认为跳表和经过优化的 `switch` 性能可能相似，但不同编译器可能会有不同的优化效果。
• **实际项目中的优化经验**：psanchez 分享了自己在一个小型布尔表达式解析器中的优化经验，包括避免字符串分配、状态化解析、最小化内存分配、使用查找表和内联字面量解析等。
• **对 lexer 优化的必要性存疑**：norir 和 aappleby 认为 lexer 通常不是性能瓶颈，因此不一定要对其进行深度优化。aappleby 更希望看到“可读性高的 lexer 策略”。

争议焦点：
• **是否需要对 lexer 进行深度优化**：一些人认为 lexer 通常不是性能瓶颈，因此不值得进行过多优化；而另一些人则分享了通过各种技术手段（如 SIMD、跳表、完美哈希）来提升 lexer 性能的具体方法和实际项目中的效果。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• **对实际应用场景的考虑**：thechao 和 psanchez 都提到了在实际项目中对 lexer 进行优化的具体需求和场景，比如流式数据处理和简洁的单文件实现。
• **对 benchmark 和实际性能影响的关注**：duped 提出了对跳表优化实际效果的疑问，并要求提供相关 benchmark 数据。

总结：讨论围绕 lexer 优化的多种技术展开，包括 `musttail` 属性、完美哈希函数、SIMD 加速等，同时有人对 lexer 优化的必要性提出质疑，强调应根据实际应用场景和性能需求进行优化。

In this blog post I’ll explain strategies I used to make the purple garden
lexer really fast.
purple-garden
is an s-expr based
language I am currently developing for myself. Its my attempt at building a
language I like, with a battery included approach, while designing it with
performance in mind.
This doesn’t mean all approaches are feasible for your use case, architecture
and design. I tried to bring receipts for my performance claims, so
watch out for these blocks at the end of chapters:
Info - Benchmark
Introduction to Lexing
A lexer (often also referred to as a tokeniser) is the easiest part of any compilation and
language pipeline. The idea is to convert a list of characters into a list of
tokens in which each token conveys some meaning. This list of tokens can then
be used by the parser to generate an abstract syntax tree (AST), which the
compiler consumes, converting it to bytecode, which the vm executes.
A compilation pipeline
As an overview:
┌───────────────────┐
│                   │
│       Lexer       │ <- we are here
│                   │
└─────────┬─────────┘
│
│ Tokens <- and here
│
┌─────────▼─────────┐
│                   │
│       Parser      │
│                   │
└─────────┬─────────┘
│
│ AST
│
┌─────────▼─────────┐
│                   │
│      Compiler     │
│                   │
└─────────┬─────────┘
│
│ Bytecode
│
┌─────────▼─────────┐
│                   │
│  Virtual Machine  │
│                   │
└───────────────────┘
For a list of characters, lets say
(@std.fmt.println "my pi is: " 3.1415)
:

TEXT

Defining purple garden’s Tokens
A token is not only a set characters it can be mapped to, but it also holds:
A token type, to easily distinguish between tokens

start point
end or length
line number

• **是否需要对 lexer 进行深度优化**：一些人认为 lexer 通常不是性能瓶颈，因此不值得进行过多优化；而另一些人则分享了通过各种技术手段（如 SIMD、跳表、完美哈希）来提升 lexer 性能的具体方法和实际项目中的效果。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• **对实际应用场景的考虑**：thechao 和 psanchez 都提到了在实际项目中对 lexer 进行优化的具体需求和场景，比如流式数据处理和简洁的单文件实现。
• **对 benchmark 和实际性能影响的关注**：duped 提出了对跳表优化实际效果的疑问，并要求提供相关 benchmark 数据。

总结：讨论围绕 lexer 优化的多种技术展开，包括 `musttail` 属性、完美哈希函数、SIMD 加速等，同时有人对 lexer 优化的必要性提出质疑，强调应根据实际应用场景和性能需求进行优化。

data.title: Lossless Float Image Compression
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了2021年和2023年对OpenEXR无损压缩选项及浮点数据压缩的研究，特别关注多通道图像（如电影制作中的多层图像），这些图像包含RGB以外的多种通道（如深度、法线等），且通常为FP16或FP32浮点数据。作者对比了OpenEXR的ZIP压缩与即将推出的HTJ2K压缩模式，发现HTJ2K压缩比稍好但性能较差。此外，JPEG-XL在压缩此类图像时不如OpenEXR。作者还提出一种自定义压缩方法，表现优于EXR和JPEG-XL，且速度更快。实验使用多组Blender渲染的EXR文件，测试了压缩比与压缩/解压缩性能。最终建议继续使用OpenEXR的ZIP压缩，同时期待HTJ2K的未来改进。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：浮点压缩技术及其相关工具和优化方法

不同观点：
• NooneAtAll3认为，在作者的浮点压缩系列文章中，图表的坐标轴被切换，使得将速度放在纵轴上看起来更简单或更优雅。这可能只是个人偏好，但表明了不同人在可视化数据时的习惯差异。

• willvarfar提到，将一个压缩器与另一个压缩器链式组合使用，让他联想到QOI（一种PNG的竞争格式）。QOI的输出在经过zstd或gzip等通用压缩工具处理之前，常常可以与PNG（使用gzip压缩）相媲美。这表明在特定情况下，链式组合压缩器可以提高压缩效果。

• kevingadd指出，文中提到的网格优化器的性能提醒人们，尽管通用压缩技术已经非常先进且难以超越，但在特定用途上仍有改进空间。这表明特定用途的压缩技术仍有发展潜力。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了不同压缩工具和技术的比较，例如QOI与PNG、zstd与gzip。这些工具在不同应用场景中的表现引发了关于通用和专用压缩技术的相对优点的讨论。

• 争议的焦点可能在于通用压缩技术是否真的难以超越，以及在特定领域中专用压缩技术的潜力到底有多大。不同评论者对压缩技术的未来发展和优化方向有不同的看法。

44523876.article_content:
Back in 2021 I looked at
OpenEXR lossless compression
options
(and I think
my findings led a change of the default
zip compression level
, as well as change of the compression library from
zlib to libdeflate
. Yay blogging about things!)
. Then in 2023 I looked
at losslessly compressing a bunch of
floating point data
, some of which might be image-shaped.
Well, now a discussion somewhere else has nerd-sniped me to look into
lossless
compression of
floating point
images,
and especially the ones that might have more than just RGB(A) color channels.
Read on!
Four bullet point summary, if you’re in a hurry:
Keep on using OpenEXR with ZIP
compression.
Soon OpenEXR might add HTJ2K compression; that compresses slightly better but is worse compression
and
decompression performance, so YMMV.
JPEG-XL is not competitive
with OpenEXR in this area today.
You
can
cook up a “custom image compression” that seems to be better than all of EXR, EXR HTJ2K and JPEG-XL, while also being way faster.
My use case and the data set
What I wanted to primarily look at, are “multi-layer” images that would be used for film composition workflows. In such an image, a single pixel
does not have just the typical RGB (and possibly alpha) channels, but might have more. Ambient occlusion, direct lighting, indirect lighting,
depth, normal, velocity, object ID, material ID, and so on. And the data itself is almost always floating point values (either FP16 or FP32);
sometimes with different precision for different channels within the same image.
There does not seem to be a readily available “standard image set” like that to test things on, so I grabbed some that I could find, and some
I have rendered myself out of various
Blender splash screen files
. Here’s the 10
data files I’m testing on (total uncompressed pixel size: 3122MB):
File
Resolution
Uncompressed size
Channels
Sample
Blender281rgb16.exr
3840x2160
47.5MB
RGB half
Blender281rgb32.exr
3840x2160
94.9MB
RGB float
Blender281layered16.exr
3840x2160
332.2MB
21 channels, half
Blender281layered32.exr
3840x2160
664.5MB
21 channels, float
Blender35.exr
3840x2160
332.2MB
18 channels, mixed half/float
Blender40.exr

348.0MB
15 channels, mixed half/float
Blender41.exr

743.6MB
37 channels, mixed half/float
Blender43.exr
3840x2160
47.5MB
RGB half
ph_brown_photostudio_02_8k.exr
8192x4096
384.0MB
RGB float, from
polyhaven
ph_golden_gate_hills_4k.exr
4096x2048
128.0MB
RGBA float, from
polyhaven
OpenEXR
OpenEXR
is an image file format that has existed since 1999, and is primarily used within film, vfx and
game industries. It has several lossless compression modes (see my
previous blog post series
).
It looks like OpenEXR 3.4 (should be out 2025 Q3) is adding a new
HTJ2K
compression mode, which is based on
“
High-Throughput JPEG 2000
” format/algorithms, using open source
OpenJPH
library. The new mode is already in OpenEXR main branch
(
PR #2041
).
So here’s how EXR does on my data set
(click for a larger interactive chart)
:
This is two plots: compression ratio vs. compression performance, and compression ratio vs. decompression performance.
In both cases, the best place on the chart is top right – the largest compression ratio, and the best performance.
For performance, I’m measuring it in GB/s, in terms of
uncompressed data size
. That is, if we have 1GB worth of raw image
pixel data and processing it took half a second, that’s 2GB/s throughput (even if
compressed data size
might be different).
Note that the vertical scale of both graphs is different. I am measuring compression/decompression time without actual disk I/O,
for simplicity – that is, I am “writing” and “reading” “files” from memory. The graph is from a run on Apple MacBookPro M4 Max,
with things being compiled in “Release” build configuration using Xcode/clang 16.1.
Green dot is EXR ZIP at default compression level (which is 4, but changing the level does not affect things much). Blue dot is the new
EXR HTJ2K compression – a bit better compression ratio, but also lower performance
. Hmm dunno, not very impressive? However:
From what I understand, HTJ2K achieves better ratio on RGB images by applying a de-correlation transform. In case of multi-layer EXR
files (which is most of my data set), it only does that for one layer (usually the “final color” one), but does not try to do that
on, for example, “direct diffuse” layer which is also “actually RGB colors”. Maybe future work within OpenEXR HTJ2K will improve this?
Initial HTJ2K evaluation
done in 2024
found that a
commercial HTJ2K implementation (from
Kakadu
) is quite a bit faster than the OpenJPH that is used in
OpenEXR. Maybe future work within OpenJPH will speed it up?
It very well might be that once/if OpenEXR will get
lossy
HTJ2K, things would be much more interesting. But that is a whole another topic.
I was testing OpenEXR main branch code from 2025 June (3.4.0-dev, rev
45ee12752
), and things are multi-threaded via
Imf::setGlobalThreadCount()
. Addition of HTJ2K

data.title: Self-imposed ban – a lightweight bash script to block commands
data.author: alex-moon
data.article_summary: "ban" 是一个轻量级的 Bash 脚本，帮助用户在指定日期前禁止自己运行浪费时间的命令，支持添加原因和友好的提醒。适合希望提升专注力的开发者。安装方法是将脚本下载到 `~/bin` 目录并赋予执行权限。使用时可以指定命令、原因和禁止期限，默认期限为40天。解除禁止只需删除对应文件。如需卸载，删除脚本和 `~/.bans` 目录即可。项目遵循MIT许可证，欢迎贡献代码和建议。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过技术手段限制某些命令的使用及其相关工具的功能和实用性

不同观点：
• [teddyh] 通过一个寓言式的对话，展示了限制某些行为（如吃饼干）的思路，类似于通过技术手段限制某些命令的使用。
• [samrus] 认为使用终端时，命令行不应该像娱乐或社交媒体那样让人分心，因此对通过“家长控制”方式限制命令使用感到不解。
• [nektro] 希望README文件能展示使用被禁命令时的示例，并指出该工具更适合防止误操作（如禁止使用`rm`命令），而不是仅仅防止分心。
• [jmholla] 质疑工具对Zenity的依赖，认为终端应用不应有GUI依赖，尤其是在无头系统（headless systems）上，建议将Zenity设为可选项，并使用STDERR作为替代。
• [ramses0] 赞赏项目的创意，指出虽然可以轻易绕过限制，但这种方法可以让人反思自己的使用习惯，并建议增加自动失效功能。
• [RS-232] 和 [priyashpatil] 以幽默的方式提出如果禁止“ban”命令本身会产生什么后果，暗示自我限制工具可能带来的悖论。
• [nikolayasdf123] 认为该工具类似于苹果系统中的“应用/时间限制”功能，肯定了其潜在价值。
• [skeptrune] 单纯觉得这个想法有趣，没有深入讨论。
• [msgodel] 分享了自己写的类似软件，专注于限制每天在某些网站上花费的时间，并认为这种简单工具可以显著改善生活。
• [foxinsocks5] 以幽默方式询问如果禁止`rm`命令会产生什么后果。

补充讨论：
- 工具的实际应用场景存在争议，一部分人认为限制命令行使用是多余的，而另一部分人则认为这在某些情况下（如防止误操作）可能非常有用。
- 对工具依赖Zenity的讨论，提出了对无头系统兼容性的担忧。
- 有人提到该工具的限制很容易被绕过，但也有观点认为这种工具的价值在于让人反思自己的行为习惯。
- 讨论中多次出现幽默和自嘲式的评论，显示出社区对这种“自我限制”工具的轻松态度。

Self-imposed ban
A lightweight Bash script to help you block yourself from using time-wasting or
distracting commands until a specified date with optional reasons and friendly reminders.
Perfect for developers and terminal junkies trying to reclaim their focus.
Install
Simply download the ban script into your
~/bin
directory or any directory in your
$PATH
and make it executable.
mkdir -p
~
/bin
curl -o
~
/bin/ban https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alex-moon/ban/refs/heads/main/ban
chmod +x
~
/bin/ban
Usage
When you ban a command, attempting to run it will result in a friendly reminder
that you have banned it, along with any reasons you provide, and a date the ban
will be lifted. Reasons and expiration dates are both optional - if the date
is not provided, the ban will expire 40 days from now.
#
these are all valid commands:
ban steam
ban steam
'
I have been spending too much time playing games
'
ban steam
'
I have been spending too much time playing games
'
2025-08-20
To unban a command, simply remove the command from your
~/.bans
directory:
rm
~
/.bans/steam
To see a list of all your current bans, simply index the
~/.bans
directory:
ls
~
/.bans
Uninstall
To uninstall the ban script, simply remove the
ban
file from your
~/bin
directory
and delete the
~/.bans
directory.
rm
~
/bin/ban
rm -rf
~
/.bans
Contributing
Contributions are welcome! If you have suggestions for improvements or new features,
please open an issue or submit a pull request.

data.title: Lenovo Legion Go S: Windows 11 vs. SteamOS Performance, and General Availability
data.author: ekianjo
data.article_summary: 文章主要对比了联想Legion Go S的两个版本：SteamOS版和Windows 11版。硬件配置相似，但SteamOS版价格更低，性能表现更好，在多款大型游戏中的帧率普遍比Windows 11版高出20-30%。同时，SteamOS版在电池续航上也更具优势，多数游戏下续航时间延长15-20%。尽管Windows 11版在反作弊游戏如《GTA 5 Online》和《APEX Legends》上有优势，但总体来看，SteamOS版性价比更高。然而，联想官网主要推广Windows版，SteamOS版很难找到，甚至在一些国家网站上未被提及。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：硬件性能、操作系统选择及其对游戏体验的影响

不同观点：
• jauntywundrkind 强调开源软件和Mesa驱动带来的性能提升，特别是Radeon软件团队转向开源栈的组织变动。他还提到Legion Go S的硬件规格和价格优势，以及对资源消耗统计的需求。
• POM37 认为尽管Steam OS在手持游戏设备上是更好的选择，但由于Frame Generation功能的缺失，他们仍然使用Windows系统。他们强调Frame Generation在提升游戏帧数和流畅度上的关键作用。
• Night_Thastus 提到微软最近的游戏平台战略，希望Windows的性能问题能因此得到改善。
• tines 表达了对Linux和Mac系统的偏好，并批评Windows开始菜单中的广告。
• magicalhippo 对Cyberpunk 2077在性能和电池寿命上的提升表示兴趣，并讨论了性能提升与能耗之间的关系。
• trelane 怀疑厂商更倾向于推广Windows版本而非SteamOS版本，并引用历史案例说明PC厂商受限于微软的OEM授权。
• staticman2 提到了2022年Steam Deck早期型号的一些使用问题，希望新设备能解决这些问题。
• acd 认为如果Linux能带来更好的FPS，玩家会愿意切换操作系统。

We have already covered it ahead of its launch: the
Lenovo Legion Go S
is a high-end handheld PC that comes in two flavors: a
SteamOS
variant and a
Windows 11
version. Today, we are going to look at the performance across both versions, based on multiple benchmarks collected from different sources on the webs.
The Lenovo Legion Go S: SteamOS for the Masses
Both versions of the
Legion Go S
use a similar AMD processor (Z2 Go at 4c/8t) and a 55.5 Wh battery, but the
SteamOS
model is priced about
$130 lower
(~$599 vs ~$730), officially. This being said, the
Windows
version can be found cheaper in some places (I seem to recall Bestbuy having it at 600 USD as well). On top of the Z2 Go processor, there is a version with the Z1 Extreme APU as well, if your wallet has more depth to it.
Since the hardware is identical, the performance of both versions is driven by the underlying software stack (OS, hardware support, and drivers).
Gaming Performance on AAA Titles
SteamOS vs Windows 11: FPS
Multiple 2025 benchmarks show the
SteamOS Legion Go S outperforms the Windows 11 version
across numerous AAA games. There is not always a huge difference, but it’s always in the same direction: equivalent or better on
SteamOS
. Note that the below numbers are a mix of different hardware and different testing conditions (Some used the Z2 Go APU, others the Z1 Extreme), but at the end it does not really matter: the trend is pretty much the same across numerous conditions observed.

More expensive

We are just pretending to release a SteamOS version but in fact we advertise the Windows model ever

data.article_summary: 英国卡迪夫大学的研究团队计划通过VERVE任务探测金星云层中的微生物生命迹象。金星大气中发现的磷化氢和氨可能暗示生物活动，因为这些气体在地球上仅由生物过程产生。由于金星表面环境极端，生命可能存在于云层中的宜居区域。VERVE探测器将搭载欧洲空间局的EnVision任务，对金星大气进行独立调查，重点搜索磷化氢、氨等可能表明生命存在的氢基气体。此前磷化氢的发现曾引发争议，后续研究将进一步验证这些发现。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：金星是否存在微生物生命及其可能性、生命来源的猜测、科学探索任务的设想、对科学发现的态度和反应

不同观点：
• acjohnson55认为金星云层中的微生物生命有可能源自地球，可能是由于重大撞击事件将地球的碎片送入太空并最终被金星捕获，微生物可能在旅途中存活并在金星大气中恢复代谢和繁殖。
• ilamont关注氨气的生成过程，指出在地球上氨气可以通过Haber-Bosch反应等化学过程大量生产，并提供了一个关于该过程的参考链接。
• pavel_lishin建议进行金星样本返回任务，设想一个探测器下降到金星大气中，通过气球悬浮采集样本，然后发射火箭返回地球或与轨道器会合，类似于计划中的火星样本返回任务。
• waltbosz以科幻故事的方式提出一种假设，即科学家带回金星的微生物进行研究，结果微生物逃逸并迅速繁殖，最终毁灭地球生命，或者这些微生物是金星文明遗留的生命形式，旨在寄生外来探险者。

补充讨论：
• munchler对金星大气中是否确实存在磷化氢提出质疑，指出该声明在几年前首次发布时曾引起很大争议。
• BSOhealth提出一个理论性问题，询问是否存在某种概率理论，认为生命存在于太阳系中的可能性与距离太阳的距离有关，类似于一个筛选机制，并询问金发姑娘区（Goldilocks zones）的数学原理。
• samuel对可能的发现表示感慨，认为如果确认金星存在微生物生命，那么唯一未解的重大谜题将是宇宙中是否存在智能生命。
• blinkbat抱怨网站上的广告体验糟糕，但未涉及讨论主题。
• webdevver以调侃的方式建议通过极限运动和商业赞助来探索金星，认为科学探索难以引起公众兴趣，并设想了一个宣传噱头。

争议焦点：
• 金星大气中磷化氢的存在是否已得到确认，munchler指出了科学界的争议。
• 金星微生物生命的可能来源，acjohnson55提出了源自地球的假设，而waltbosz则以科幻故事的形式提出了另一种可能性。

这些观点和讨论展示了关于金星潜在生命的多种假设和科学探索的不同设想，同时也反映了对科学发现和探索的不同态度。

An artistâs impression of the proposed VERVE mission to Venus the answer whether tiny bacterial lifeforms really do exist in the planetâs clouds.
Â© Danielle Futselaar
A UK-based mission is aiming to settle, once and for all, whether life exists on Venus. The mission plans to send a probe to the planet in search of microbial life, not on the surface, of course, but in the Venusian clouds.
Over the past half-decade, scientists have detected the presence of phosphine and ammoniaâtwo potential signs of biological activityâin Venusâs clouds. On Earth, both gases are produced only by biological activity and industrial processes, and scientists are unsure of their origin on Venus.
Given the planetâs thick, toxic atmosphere, scorching surface temperatures, and crushing surface pressure, a booming industrial economy seems unlikely. But microbesâwhich can thrive in Earthâs hottest, most toxic environmentsâmight be able to survive on Venus and produce these gases, researchers posit.
âOur latest data has found more evidence of ammonia on Venus, with the potential for it to exist in the habitable parts of the planetâs clouds,â Jane Greaves, an astronomer at the University of Cardiff, said in a
statement
. âThere are no known chemical processes for the production of either ammonia or phosphine, so the only way to know for sure what is responsible for them is to go there.â
At this yearâs
Royal Astronomical Society National Astronomy
Meeting, researchers from the University of Cardiff presented their plan to search for and map phosphine, ammonia, and other hydrogen-rich gases that might indicate the presence of microbial life on Earthâs twin.
The mission, called the Venus Explorer for Reduced Vapours in the Environment (VERVE), will send a CubeSat-sized probe aboard the European Space Agencyâs EnVision missionâa larger mission designed to probe Venusâs surface and interior, scheduled for launch in 2031. VERVE will detach upon arrival and carry out an independent atmospheric survey.
Researchers first detected phosphine in Venusâs clouds in 2020. The finding was controversial, however, as follow-up studies failed to replicate the results.
But a subsequent project, JCMTâVenus, designed to study the molecular composition of Venusâs atmosphere using the James Clerk Maxwell Telescope in Hawaii, offered a possible explanation for these disparate findings. Researchers tracked the phosphine signature over time and found it could only be detected at night, as it was destroyed by sunlight. They also discovered that the amount of gas in Venusâs atmosphere varied over time.
Last year, at the National Astronomy Meeting, researchers also reported the detection of ammonia in Venusâs atmosphere.
Although surface temperatures on Venus reach around 450 degrees Celsius, conditions become much more reasonable about 31 miles (50 kilometers) above the surface, where temperatures range from 30 degrees Celsius to 70 degrees Celsius. Researchers believe it may be possible for extremophilesâlike those found in Earthâs hydrothermal vents and deep-sea trenchesâto survive in these conditions.

不同观点：
• **赞赏公司工作**：[evanjrowley] 称赞该公司的工作，特别是提到他们推荐并帮助家人设置的 Beelink SER8 迷你电脑运行良好，表明对该公司产品质量和组织能力的认可。

• **对技术操作的质疑**：[alargemoose] 对视频中约14分钟时将CMOS电池粘住的行为表示不解，认为这种做法不妥，因为CMOS电池的寿命通常短于PC的有效使用寿命，对这种选择感到意外。

• **提供无广告链接**：[ProllyInfamous] 没有直接参与观点讨论，而是提供了一个无广告的视频链接，方便其他人观看。

• **对人工操作和技术细节的观察**：[LargoLasskhyfv] 注意到视频中更多的人工操作，并对方便临时使用的CPU散热器在首次POST过程中即插即用的做法表示兴趣，认为这种方法虽然冒险但似乎在生产/测试的特定步骤中是可靠的。同时，还提到视频中使用了Crucial内存条，但对SSD的型号无法识别。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：主要的争议在于视频中粘住CMOS电池的做法是否合理，[alargemoose] 认为这种做法会影响PC的长期使用，而其他评论者未对此做出直接回应。

• **技术细节的关注**：[LargoLasskhyfv] 对视频中的技术细节如CPU散热器的临时应用和硬件品牌表现出浓厚兴趣，显示出对实际操作细节的关注。

data.title: The Tokyo capsule tower that gave pod-living penthouse chic
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary:
**总结：**

东京的中银胶囊塔（Nakagin Capsule Tower）由日本激进建筑师黑川纪章设计，1972年建成，成为当时轰动一时的建筑奇迹。该建筑由140个小型胶囊组成，每个胶囊配备现代化设施，如独立浴室、折叠桌、电话和彩电，最初作为都市白领临时居住的豪华舱，而非全职住宅。由于年久失修和业主间的分歧，该建筑于2022年被拆除。然而，部分胶囊被修复，并于2023年在纽约现代艺术博物馆（MoMA）展出，通过沉浸式展览重现其历史与设计理念。黑川纪章曾将胶囊建筑比作汽车，具备从办公室到都市别墅的多功能用途，展现了未来主义的生活方式。

44559857.article_content:
Cocoon yourself away … Nakagin Capsule Tower, which caused a sensation.
Photograph: Tomio Ohashi
View image in fullscreen
Cocoon yourself away … Nakagin Capsule Tower, which caused a sensation.
Photograph: Tomio Ohashi
Architecture
‘As thrilling as driving a sports car’: the Tokyo capsule tower that gave pod-living penthouse chic
They had portholes, cutting edge mod cons – and the ultra luxurious models even came with a free calculator. As Japan’s beloved Nakagin Capsule Tower resurfaces, we celebrate an architectural marvel
Oliver Wainwright
Mon 7 Jul 2025 00.00 EDT
Last modified on Mon 7 Jul 2025 12.38 EDT
Share
L
ooking like a teetering stack of washing machines perched on the edge of an elevated highway, the Nakagin Capsule Tower was an astonishing arrival on the Tokyo skyline in 1972. It was the heady vision of
Kisho Kurokawa
, a radical Japanese architect who imagined a high-rise world of compact capsules, where people could cocoon themselves away from the information overload of the modern age. These tiny pods would be “a place of rest to recover”, he wrote, as well as “an information base to develop ideas, and a home for urban dwellers”. Residents could peer out at the city from their cosy built-in beds through a single porthole window, or shut it all out by unfurling an elegant circular fan-like blind, all while remaining connected with the latest technology at all times.
Launched to critical acclaim, the Nakagin tower’s 140 capsules quickly sold out, and became highly sought after by well-heeled salarymen looking for a place to crash when they missed the last train home. Never intended to be full-time housing, the pods came stuffed with mod cons: en suite bathroom, foldout desk, telephone and Sony colour TV. But, 50 years on, after a prolonged lack of maintenance and repairs, and disagreements among owners about its future, the asbestos-riddled building was finally disassembled in 2022. The creaking steel capsules of Kurokawa’s space-age fantasy were unbolted and removed from the lift and stair towers, pod by pod.
Buildings in Tokyo had an average lifespan of 15 to 20 years. So standing for 50 years makes it a resounding success
Now, three years on, a little piece of his dream is back. After a meticulous process of conservation, people will soon be able to get a glimpse of life in one of these sci-fi capsules, thanks to a
new exhibition
at the Museum of Modern Art in New York. MoMA acquired a unit in 2023, one of 14 capsules that were carefully restored to their original condition, with oversight from Kurokawa’s office, after the tower was disassembled. “The Nakagin Capsule Tower is one of the world’s most written about works of modern architecture,” says MoMA curator Evangelos Kotsioris. “But the many lives of the building, and its residents, have rarely been told.”
View image in fullscreen
‘Office, studio, hotel, home, conference room, or urban villa’ … interior view.
Photograph: © Noritaka Minami
He and co-curator Paula Vilaplana de Miguel have pieced together an immersive display that tells the full story of the project in all its facets, from conception to marketing to unexpected afterlife. There will be a wealth of ephemera, from the building’s only surviving sales brochure, to the original promotional film for the tower, alongside video interviews with former residents, and an explorable digital model of the entire building. And of course, there’s the capsule itself, visible in all its freshly white-painted glory through the window of MoMA’s street-level gallery. The museum’s retractable glass facade was opened up for the first time to get it in.
Peek through the pod’s porthole window and you will find a streamlined white world that could have been lifted from 2001: A Space Odyssey. A reel-to-reel tape recorder shines out from an angled wall panel, next to a sleek radio receiver and built-in rotary phone, beneath a Sony Trinitron TV. A bright red Olivetti typewriter perches on a fold-down desk, alongside a Sharp electronic calculator – one of the cutting-edge features included in the “super-deluxe” capsule model.
“Just as there is a full range of automobiles, from sedans to coupes to sports cars,” Kurokawa explained in the sales brochure, “a capsule house can serve numerous purposes – mini-office, studio, hotel, home, conference room, or urban villa – based on the equipment selected.”
View image in fullscreen
Media-savvy salesman … Kurokawa in front of the completed tower in 1974.
Photograph: Tomio Ohashi
Kurokawa was the youngest founding member of the
Metabolist movement
, a group of Japanese architects formed in 1960 that fused ideas about megastructures with those of organic biological growth. They imagined a networked world of interconnecting modular structures that could multiply and spread across the planet like a great branching fungus. data.title: MacPaint Art from the Mid-80s Still Looks Great Today
data.author: decryption
data.article_summary: 这篇文章分享了作者浏览BMUG的CD-ROM中1980年代中期使用MacPaint软件创作的艺术作品的体验。作者查看了超过18,000张MacPaint图片，并对这些早期计算机艺术作品表示赞赏，认为即使在今天看来仍很出色。文章提到希望找到这些艺术家，了解他们目前的成就。作者还比较了同时期的Amiga电脑，认为其也能创作类似甚至更好的艺术作品，并计划进一步探索。文章最后推荐了一本名为《Zen & The Art of The Macintosh》的书，供读者学习当时的创作技巧。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕早期数字艺术工具和其艺术价值的讨论，特别是MacPaint等老式工具创作的像素艺术。

不同观点：
• seabombs认为，艺术作品的“审美完整性”不依赖于图形硬件的进步，早期游戏如Homeworld就是例子。使用当时的工具创作的艺术作品是独特的，改变工具会使作品完全不同。
• WoodenChair提供了将现代照片转换为MacPaint风格的工具链接，并提及自己书籍中对相关编程技术的介绍。
• gxd指出，Amiga上的Deluxe Paint也创造了独特的艺术风格，早期计算机的限制形成了独特的艺术表现形式。
• hcarvalhoalves认为，这些作品的伟大之处在于艺术家的传统绘画技巧，如交叉影线和透视法，这些技巧独立于数字媒介的先进性。
• aresant提到了一位仍在创作MacPaint像素艺术的艺术家Pinot，认为其作品应被包括在讨论中。
• poisonborz表达了对过去计算机爱好者热情的怀念，认为那时人们更多地考虑彼此的利益。
• HPsquared用洞穴壁画作类比，说明古代艺术至今仍具欣赏价值。
• rswail引用Charles Eames的名言，强调设计在于限制，Mac和MacPaint的限制形成了特定时代的艺术形式。
• kjellsbells指出某些作品的作者身份，并提到相关社区对这种艺术形式的讨论。
• taylorius认为，非照片级的逼真度让观众用想象力填补空白，促进了与内容的某种互动。
• decryption补充了更多一比特像素艺术图片以满足讨论的热度。
• cjcenizal分享了个人对早期像素艺术的怀旧情感，这些作品唤起了童年的记忆。
• reconnecting提供了与老式计算机兼容的网站链接，并询问Netscape 4的缺点。
• Mizza对某件作品与“View of the World from 9th Avenue”的相似性提出看法，并对Acius历史进行了解释。
• cubefox对某件街景像素艺术作品给予高度评价。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中提到了Netscape 4的兼容性问题，以及对老式计算机和软件的怀旧情感。
• 争议的焦点可能在于艺术作品的伟大究竟是源于工具的限制还是艺术家的技巧，不同评论者有各自的侧重。
• 链接和资源分享为想深入了解或亲自尝试创作此类艺术的读者提供了实践途径。

44540402.article_content:
MacPaint Art From The Mid-80s Still Looks Great Today
July 12, 2025
I really enjoyed browsing the
BMUG's CD-ROM and discovering early 80s art made in MacPaint
, so I browsed all 18,000+ MacPaint images on
Discmaster
to see what gems I can unearth. Here is some what I found.
Would be cool to try track down some of these artists and see what they're up to these days. If they could do this type of work on those little 9-inch, 1-bit screens 40 years ago, I'd love to see what they've achieved since.
The Amiga was another computer around the same time that could do similar (arguably better) levels of computer art at home, so I think I'll explore that soon. Could be some cool stuff there!
Lots of people like this post!
Here's some of the less spectacular art (e.g: not designed so much to be art in and of itself) but still cool logos, graphics, icons and the like. If you'd like to see more, just visit the wonderful
Discmaster
and use the search feature to find images by file type. MacPaint, MacDraw or any other old graphics program (perhaps even Photoshop files dated before 1990 or something?) should surface thousands of pieces from this era and in this style.
This is just a collection of smaller icons I liked, dumped into a single canvas:
If you'd like to create art like this there's a wonderful book called Zen & The Art of The Macintosh available on the Internet Archive that explains the techniques (and more) of the time. This book deserves a post all of its own IMHO so I won't spoil it for you:

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：多模型单聊应用的可行性、定价模式的透明度、现有工具和替代方案的比较

不同观点：
• al_borland支持多模型单聊应用，并提到Kagi Assistant已经解决了其需求，但认为信用模型和定价不够透明。他希望了解1,000 tokens或100 credits能带来的具体使用预期，并倾向于按需付费的模式。
• mritchie712和fredwu表示没有找到合适的工具，因此自行开发了一个。fredwu还质疑是否充分尝试过使用Google搜索类似服务。
• kwamenum86推荐Librechat，称其为开源且被大公司使用的工具，已经过实战检验。
• woodylondon分享了其一年前的类似探索，最终选择了TypingMind，认为其提供了多LLM支持和集中管理功能。
• vinhnx介绍了自己开发的VT平台，强调安全和隐私，支持BYOK和本地模型。
• bearjaws指出已经有许多类似产品，并列举了多个竞争者，认为没有必要重复开发。
• Alifatisk和yellow_lead分别提到OpenRouter和t3.chat作为替代方案。
• covercash询问是否有聊天机器人可以根据查询建议最佳LLM。
• lemming强调了网络搜索功能的重要性，认为这是ChatGPT的杀手级功能，而替代品和开源选项无法提供。
• intellectronica指出已经有很多多模型访问工具，如Raycast和Poe，对自行开发表示不解。
• swores询问是否存在开源的OpenRouter替代品，并希望使用标准非AI聊天应用作为界面。
• k9294以loqus.ai的共同创始人身份分享了经验，认为大多数人并不需要多个模型和自定义指令，ChatGPT已经满足了大多数需求，因此停止了类似工具的开发。

data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 加州理工学院的研究团队开发了一种利用二氧化碳、水和电力生产塑料的系统。该系统通过电化学反应将二氧化碳转化为乙烯和一氧化碳，然后将这些分子引入第二个催化循环，生成聚酮类塑料。这些塑料具有高强度、耐用性和热稳定性，适用于粘合剂、汽车零件、体育用品和工业管道等多种应用。与以往系统不同，该系统不依赖石油副产品提供乙烯，而是直接从二氧化碳中获取。该团队解决了此前二氧化碳转化过程中乙烯和一氧化碳产量低的问题，实现了11%的乙烯和14%的一氧化碳浓度。该系统分为两个步骤，分别在不同的反应环境中高效运作，为人工光合作用和塑料生产提供了新途径。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：将二氧化碳（CO2）转化为有用材料的生产经济性和环境影响

• xgkickt和crocowhile对增加塑料生产持批评态度，暗示这可能导致环境问题，如微塑料导致的大规模灭绝。
• rbanffy指出，许多问题可以通过能源解决，暗示技术进步可以应对环境挑战。
• hofo质疑是否需要更多的塑料，尽管这种技术可以不依赖石油生产塑料。
• exabrial建议将CO2转化为建筑材料，如CO2砖，以实现更快的碳捕捉。
• ltbarcly3解释了塑料的基本成分，强调传统塑料生产与现代技术的相似性。

• metalman详细讨论了CO2转化过程中的实际挑战，包括副产品和沉积物的处理，以及高纯度产品的生产成本。
• commienews质疑反向过程的可能性，即从塑料中生产水和电。
• mdaniel用幽默的方式表达了对未来技术的期待，提到生物体消化CO2生成石油的可能性。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是增加塑料生产的环境影响，特别是微塑料对生态系统的潜在危害。
• 另一个讨论点是技术可行性和经济性，包括催化剂的改进和生产成本的控制。
• 有人提到需要通过法规和补贴来促进环保技术的应用，以应对市场无法自行解决的长期损害问题。

Credit:

(2025). DOI: 10.1002/anie.202503003
What if a machine could suck up carbon dioxide from the atmosphere, run it through a series of chemical reactions, and essentially spit out industrially useful plastic?
"I think that is something that we, as a society, would be interested in. After all, in addition to being a
greenhouse gas
, carbon dioxide is an abundant and inexpensive feedstock," says Theo Agapie, Ph.D., the John Stauffer Professor of Chemistry and the executive officer for chemistry at Caltech. "With our new work, we have taken a significant step in that direction."
Reporting
in the journal
Angewandte Chemie International Edition
, Agapie and a team of Caltech chemists have developed a system that uses electricity from sustainable sources to carry out the chemical conversion of carbon dioxide (CO
2
) into molecules, such as ethylene and
carbon monoxide
, that are useful for making more complex compounds.
When this is accomplished using light as the energy source, without plants, such a process is known as artificial photosynthesis. The new system feeds the ethylene and carbon monoxide that have been generated into a second catalytic loop that yields industrially useful plastics called polyketones, which are known for their strength, durability, and thermal stability, making them ideal for applications ranging from adhesives to car parts and from sports equipment to industrial piping.
"We have shown that one can use CO
2
to make a material that is useful, without using plants as a mediator," says lead author Max Zhelyabovskiy, a graduate student in Agapie's lab who was co-mentored on the project by Jonas C. Peters, Caltech's Bren Professor of Chemistry and director of the Resnick Sustainability Institute.
The Caltech-led team is not the first to build a system that attempts to pair CO
2
reduction with a second chemical reaction to ultimately produce polymers. But previous systems have added ethylene that comes from petroleum products, rather than deriving it from
carbon dioxide
and water.
The conversion of CO
2
all the way to plastic has been challenging for a number of reasons. Among those is the fact that previous electrochemical CO
2
reduction systems have yielded very little ethylene and carbon monoxide, the reagents needed to feed the second step of the conversion to polyketones. In fact, most have produced less than 5% concentrations of these desired compounds, along with other undesired chemicals that can potentially harm downstream processes.
"It has been difficult, at least on the lab scale, to obtain high-concentration, high-purity streams of reagents that can then be converted into something like a plastic or a fuel," Zhelyabovskiy says. But the system he helped develop achieves significantly higher concentrations—11% ethylene and 14% carbon monoxide.
But that is not the only challenge. Coupling the two systems—one for the CO
2
reduction and another for the catalysis step that follows—is not trivial, says Zhelyabovskiy: "Most work in the literature focuses on either the first or the second step, separately and with pure feedstocks. Not both."

A two-step system
Recognizing the vastly different environments needed for the CO
2
reduction and the secondary catalytic step to operate with
high efficiency
, the Caltech team devised a system featuring two distinct loops for the separate reactions.
For the first loop, the system begins with gas diffusion electrode cells, hydrophobic polymers coated in a thin layer of copper. The scientists pump CO
2
into a gas cylinder connected to the cells and flow a potassium bicarbonate electrolyte through the cells, all while applying a voltage to the electrodes. By looping the gases through this electrochemical setup multiple times, they are able to generate relatively high concentrations of ethylene and carbon monoxide.
After about an hour of building up those gases, the researchers then feed the ethylene and carbon monoxide into the second step: a closed reactor where the gases are bubbled through a solution of a palladium catalyst. Google confirms it's 'combining' Chrome OS and Android into a single platform
This might be the first time Google has publicly confirmed plans for the platform merger.
By
Hadlee Simons

0

Ryan Haines / Android Authority
TL;DR
A Google executive has reportedly confirmed that the company will combine Chrome OS and Android into a single platform.
This news comes after we reported in November that Chrome OS will be merged into Android.
This also follows Android 16’s release, which brings several desktop-themed features to the platform.
We exclusively reported back in November that Google was working to merge
Chrome OS
into
Android
. Now, a Google executive has effectively confirmed the company’s intentions to combine the two platforms.
Sameer Samat, president of Android ecosystem at Google, asked a
TechRadar
journalist why they were using an Apple Watch, iPhone, and MacBook:
I asked because we’re going to be combining Chrome OS and Android into a single platform, and I am very interested in how people are using their laptops these days and what they’re getting done.
This might be the first time that Google has publicly acknowledged plans to merge the two platforms. The executive didn’t give any more details about the initiative, but we previously reported that Google plans to
migrate Chrome OS over to Android
rather than combining the two to create an all-new platform.
It’s also interesting to hear Samat ask people about their laptop usage in the context of this initiative. This suggests that Google is still looking for ways to improve this project ahead of its release.
Google’s plan to merge Chrome OS into Android also comes as Android itself gains several features for large displays. These additions include a proper desktop mode, desktop windowing, improved external display management features, and improved app adaptability.
What do readers think of Google’s plans, though? At the time,
almost half of all polled readers
told us that the company should merge Chrome OS into Android. However, a sizeable portion of readers felt that it was a bad move or that Google couldn’t be trusted to pull it off. Some readers also questioned whether this project could affect Chromebook updates and dramatically increase Chromebook hardware requirements. So here’s hoping these two issues in particular are adequately addressed.

44558290.article_summary: Google高管Sameer Samat首次公开确认，公司计划将Chrome OS和Android合并为一个平台。此前有报道称Chrome OS将并入Android，而不是创建一个全新平台。Android 16的发布带来了多项桌面功能，显示出Google对大屏幕设备的重视。尽管部分用户支持这一合并计划，但也有人担心这可能影响Chromebook的更新和硬件要求。Google正在关注用户对笔记本的使用情况，以完善该项目。
44558290.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Chromebook与Android安全机制的整合及其对用户自由操作设备的影响

不同观点：
• [kotaKat的观点] 担心Chromebook引入Android的强安全机制（如SafetyNet验证）会限制用户对设备的掌控。具体担忧包括无法再root设备或安装其他操作系统，并提到AOSP（Android开源项目）的限制可能会影响Chromebook的开发支持。总体认为这对Chromebook生态系统来说是个不好的变化。

• [thisgoodlife的观点] 认为过多的操作系统没有必要，甚至提出将Fuchsia（谷歌的另一个操作系统项目）整合进来，以减少操作系统的种类。这一观点似乎倾向于简化技术生态，而不是关注用户自由或设备掌控问题。

补充讨论：
- [kotaKat] 对设备自由操作的关注反映了部分用户对技术限制的不满，尤其是对开源开发和设备定制的需求。
- [thisgoodlife] 的评论则反映了另一种立场，即技术整合和简化可能带来的好处，但未深入讨论安全机制对开发者和用户自由的影响。

data.author: motorest
data.article_summary: Incus 是一个下一代系统容器、应用容器和虚拟机管理工具，提供类似公有云的用户体验，支持容器和虚拟机混合使用，共享存储和网络。它基于镜像，支持多种Linux发行版，具有灵活性和可扩展性，适用于不同硬件环境。Incus可通过命令行工具、REST API或第三方工具管理实例，具备核心API、安全性、可扩展性、事件驱动、远程使用等特性。它支持多种存储后端和网络类型，提供备份、快照和实例迁移功能，适用于Linux、Windows和macOS平台。Incus由社区驱动，是Canonical的LXD的替代方案，目前由原LXD团队维护。Incus提供长期支持版本和功能版本，采用Apache 2许可证，源代码托管于GitHub。

44539338.article_content:
Incus
Introduction
Go to Table of Contents
What is Incus?
¶
Incus is a next-generation system container, application container, and virtual machine manager.
It provides a user experience similar to that of a public cloud. With it, you can easily mix and match both containers and virtual machines, sharing the same underlying storage and network.
Incus is image based and provides images for a
wide number of Linux distributions
. It provides flexibility and scalability for various use cases, with support for different storage backends and network types and the option to install on hardware ranging from an individual laptop or cloud instance to a full server rack.
When using Incus, you can manage your instances (containers and VMs) with a simple command line tool, directly through the REST API or by using third-party tools and integrations. Incus implements a single REST API for both local and remote access.
The Incus project
was created
by Aleksa Sarai as a community driven alternative to Canonical's LXD.
Today, it's led and maintained by many of the same people that once created LXD.
Get started
¶
To get a better idea of what Incus is and what it does, you can
try it online
!
Then if you want to run it locally, take a look at our
getting started guide
.
Containers and virtual machines
¶
Incus provides support for system containers, application containers, and virtual machines.
When running a system container, Incus simulates a virtual version of a full operating system. To do this, it uses the functionality provided by the kernel running on the host system.
When running an application container, Incus runs isolated applications within the host's operating system using container images, similar to how Docker operates.
When running a virtual machine, Incus uses the hardware of the host system, but the kernel is provided by the virtual machine. Therefore, virtual machines can be used to run, for example, a different operating system.
You can learn more about the differences between application containers, system containers and virtual machines in
our documentation
.
Features
¶
Some of the biggest features of Incus are:
Core API
Secure by design
(through unprivileged containers, resource restrictions, authentication, ...)
Intuitive
(with a simple, clear API and crisp command line experience)
Scalable
(from containers on your laptop to clusters of thousands of compute nodes)
Event based
(providing logging, operation, and lifecycle events)
Remote usage
(same API used for local and network access)
Project support
(as a way to compartmentalize sets of images and profiles)
Instances and profiles
Image based
(with images for a wide variety of Linux distributions, published daily)
Instances
(containers and virtual-machines)
Configurable through profiles
(applicable to both containers and virtual machines)
Backup and export
Backup and recovery
(for all objects managed by Incus)
Snapshots
(to save and restore the state of an instance)
Container and image transfer
(between different hosts, using images)
Instance migration
(importing existing instances or transferring them between servers)
Configurability
Multiple storage backends
(with configurable storage pools and storage volumes)
Network management
(including bridge creation and configuration, cross-host tunnels, ...)
Advanced resource control
(CPU, memory, network I/O, block I/O, disk usage and kernel resources)
Device passthrough
(USB, GPU, unix character and block devices, NICs, disks and paths)
Availability
¶
Incus works on any recent Linux distribution.
Incus upstream doesn't directly provide packages, but packages are available in a number of distributions or can be found in 3rd party repositories.
In addition, the Incus client is available for Windows and macOS. You can use the client to connect to an Incus server running on a Linux machine.
Current installation instructions can be found in our
installation guide
.
Support
¶
Incus has two kind of releases:
LTS releases
Feature releases
The current LTS release is Incus 6.0 and is supported until June 2029.
Feature releases are pushed out every month or so and contain new features as well as bugfixes.
The normal support length for those releases is of about a month, or until the next release comes out.
Some Linux distributions might offer longer support for particular feature releases that they decided to ship.
Commercial support for Incus can be obtained from
Zabbly
.
Language, licensing and contributions
¶
Incus is written in Go. It is free software and developed under the
Apache 2 license
.
The Incus source code is available on
GitHub
.
There are no CLA or similar legal agreements required to contribute to Incus. However, we require commits be signed-off (following the DCO - Developer Certificate of Ownership). See the
Contribution guidelines
for more information.

Availability
Support

data.title: New Date("wtf") – How well do you know JavaScript's Date class?
data.author: OuterVale
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了使用NodeJS 24.4.0在BST时区（UTC+1）的MacBook Pro上验证的一系列问题，形成了一个包含20个问题的测验。测验由"samwho"制作，用户可以依次回答问题，最后看到自己的得分。测验结束时，用户有机会分享或复制链接。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：JavaScript日期处理的复杂性、意外行为以及可能的解决方案

不同观点：
• **JavaScript日期处理的复杂性与意外行为**：
  - [schoen] 指出JavaScript的日期解析器会以许多令人意外的方式解释输入，甚至在人类用户不会同意这些解释的情况下也是如此。
  - [norskeld] 和 [KaiMagnus] 都提到了他们在测试中遇到的“诅咒”体验，得分很低，并认为需要寻找更好的解决方案。
  - [hidroto] 认为自己的策略是尽量避免处理JavaScript的日期。

• **UTC和ISO 8601字符串作为解决方案**：
  - [mnahkies] 强调在实际应用中，应尽量使用UTC和ISO 8601字符串或Unix时间戳来简化问题，并减少复杂性。
  - [the__alchemist] 也支持使用ISO字符串，指出Moment.js在处理日期和时间上的问题。

• **JavaScript Date类的批评与历史背景**：
  - [fanf2] 认为JavaScript的Date类基本上是直接从Java移植过来的，包含了许多令人困惑的行为。
  - [vander_elst] 对JavaScript日期处理的设计过程表示疑惑，质疑这样的设计是如何形成的。

• **Temporal提案的提及**：
  - [norskeld] 提到了Temporal提案，认为这是一个检查新特性的好时机。
  - [worble] 询问是否有除Firefox之外的浏览器支持Temporal提案。

• **对JavaScript的调侃与幽默**：
  - [pluc] 开玩笑地说JavaScript会“反击”，例如通过Node变得无处不在。
  - [saghm] 幽默地表示自己的得分可能是“November 28, 2000”。
  - [torlok] 提到自己编程JavaScript超过十年，但从来不敢使用Date解析未经验证的输入。

• **对JavaScript的总体评价**：
  - [sankalpmukim] 调侃JavaScript是一种“玩具语言”，质疑如此多的重要软件是如何用它编写的。

补充讨论：
• **实用建议**：
  - [mnahkies] 给出了实用建议，建议开发者仔细考虑用例是否真的需要关心本地时间，并尽量减少处理日期复杂性的代码面积。
  
• **外部资源**：
  - [bsmth] 提供了作者Sam Rose关于此问题的文章链接。
  - [leipert] 提到JavaScript日期处理可能是实现依赖的，并提供了MDN文档链接。

争议焦点：JavaScript日期处理的复杂性和意外行为是否可以通过使用UTC和ISO 8601字符串完全避免，还是需要更根本的语言设计改进（如Temporal提案的引入）。

  - [norskeld] 和 [KaiMagnus] 都提到了他们在测试中遇到的“诅咒”体验，得分很低，并认为需要寻找更好的解决方案。
  - [hidroto] 认为自己的策略是尽量避免处理JavaScript的日期。

• **UTC和ISO 8601字符串作为解决方案**：
  - [mnahkies] 强调在实际应用中，应尽量使用UTC和ISO 8601字符串或Unix时间戳来简化问题，并减少复杂性。
  - [the__alchemist] 也支持使用ISO字符串，指出Moment.js在处理日期和时间上的问题。

• **JavaScript Date类的批评与历史背景**：
  - [fanf2] 认为JavaScript的Date类基本上是直接从Java移植过来的，包含了许多令人困惑的行为。
  - [vander_elst] 对JavaScript日期处理的设计过程表示疑惑，质疑这样的设计是如何形成的。

• **Temporal提案的提及**：
  - [norskeld] 提到了Temporal提案，认为这是一个检查新特性的好时机。
  - [worble] 询问是否有除Firefox之外的浏览器支持Temporal提案。

• **对JavaScript的调侃与幽默**：
  - [pluc] 开玩笑地说JavaScript会“反击”，例如通过Node变得无处不在。
  - [saghm] 幽默地表示自己的得分可能是“November 28, 2000”。
  - [torlok] 提到自己编程JavaScript超过十年，但从来不敢使用Date解析未经验证的输入。

• **对JavaScript的总体评价**：
  - [sankalpmukim] 调侃JavaScript是一种“玩具语言”，质疑如此多的重要软件是如何用它编写的。

补充讨论：
• **实用建议**：
  - [mnahkies] 给出了实用建议，建议开发者仔细考虑用例是否真的需要关心本地时间，并尽量减少处理日期复杂性的代码面积。
  
• **外部资源**：
  - [bsmth] 提供了作者Sam Rose关于此问题的文章链接。
  - [leipert] 提到JavaScript日期处理可能是实现依赖的，并提供了MDN文档链接。

争议焦点：JavaScript日期处理的复杂性和意外行为是否可以通过使用UTC和ISO 8601字符串完全避免，还是需要更根本的语言设计改进（如Temporal提案的引入）。

We reached $1M ARR with zero funding
Kyle Nolan

Jun 30, 2025
Bootstrapping a side project into a profitable seven-figure business in four years.
We really did it! We bootstrapped ProjectionLab to $1,000,000 in annual recurring revenue.
And I’m still processing that this is real. 🥹
Back in 2021, I was inspired by the financial independence movement and wanted a better way to plan my own life. I couldn’t find the right tool, so I started building.
I had no idea that side project would one day help over 100,000 households plan for their financial future too.
How we got here
If this is your first time hearing about ProjectionLab, here’s a quick recap:
Milestone

What Was Happening

post to HN
)

Whoah, public speaking?!

Started to believe I could do this

The final boss of indie hacking

Dropped to part-time at my day job
$23.3K MRR
Nov 2023
Quit my day job and went all-in!
$41.6K MRR
Jul 2024
Started growing the team
$45.8K MRR
Aug 2024
Shared story on ChooseFI
$83.3k MRR
Jun 2025
👋 Here we are!
When you look beyond the recurring revenue chart, this journey had ups, downs, and moments I wanted to quit.
The emotions behind the numbers
Want to know what building in public from zero to a million dollars a year really felt like? NOT like serenely progressing up-and-to-the-right…
More like riding a dopamine rollercoaster while getting attacked by a bear.
Your browser does not support the video tag.
The flat months in the early years? The dips in earnings? The times I woke up to a dozen canceled subscriptions?
Each one had me questioning everything, wondering if I should just focus on the corporate ladder, or maybe try to get into big tech instead.
The financial independence movement is what set me on this path. So on top of worrying about normal business risks, I was primed to think in terms of my time and opportunity cost, and how failure would hurt my own timeline to FI.
But gradually, I learned that emotional peaks and valleys are always a part of entrepreneurship. And that “not giving up” is actually a superpower.
Not giving up
There are loads of people out there smarter than me.
But luckily, success indexes less on IQ and more on consistency. The willingness to doggedly show up every single day can take you to some really suprising and amazing places.
And you know what makes it easier and more rewarding to be that persistent?
Working alongside people you like.
From solo dev to real team
For the first two years, I burned the candle at both ends working solo. 4-6 hours every night after work, entire weekends, holidays, you name it.
404 Day Off Not Found.
That was the only way I could build something this complex in a crowded market as a risk-averse engineer with a day job. And I was fortunate enough to attempt this at a stage in life when I had lots of energy and few family responsibilities.
Plus my trusty sidekick, BB the bird:
But long-term, I knew there would be a choice to face:
Keep doing everything myself and watch growth plateau, or…
Find someone with a complementary skillset and start building a team.
I was just an ordinary engineer with zero marketing experience. So I figured I should try to team up with someone good at growth & marketing.
Finding a growth & marketing partner
During the first few years, I was approached by dozens of potential “partners.” Several wanted an outsize equity stake to essentially just make suggestions. Others had the wrong skillset or didn’t feel like a complete fit.
But
Jon Kuipers
jumped right into the trenches and worked to prove himself before asking for anything. He spent a year contributing real value, and when the time came to bring on a growth partner full-time, I didn’t look anywhere else.
Now I stay focused on building, while he handles growth, marketing, partnerships, and some ops stuff.
Building a team
We’ve also added a few contractors to the team.
And these guys are legends. 💪
They come straight from the ProjectionLab user community, and they are doing a great job fielding the arcane finance questions our customers love to ask. Plus hosting 1-on-1 sessions, creating
tutorial videos
, and more.
Could we have offshored customer success for pennies on the dollar instead? You bet. But having a happy and engaged user community of product evangelists means a lot to us, and I want them all to have the best experience possible.
For multiple years, I was up at all hours answering support questions myself. It interrupted my dev work (and my sleep) constantly. I love the PL community – it’s a big part of what motivated me to keep going back then.

data.title: Cognition (Devin AI) to Acquire Windsurf
data.author: alazsengul
data.article_summary: Cognition已签署最终协议，收购代理集成开发环境（IDE）Windsurf。此次收购包括Windsurf的知识产权、产品、商标、品牌及业务，尤其是其顶尖的团队人才。短期内，Windsurf团队将保持现有运营，Cognition将专注于利用Devin加速工程开发。未来几个月，Cognition将大力投资，将Windsurf的独特功能整合至其产品中。此次收购旨在强化Cognition在软件工程领域的未来发展，双方团队将共同努力实现这一目标。Windsurf员工将全部参与财务分配，并获得尊重和妥善安置。Cognition期待通过此次收购加快其使命的实现，推动工程师从基础工作转向系统设计。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：科技公司收购、人才争夺以及AI技术发展的合理性与泡沫问题

不同观点：
• **泡沫论**：[pm90] 认为当前的科技公司交易动荡表明市场可能正处于一个与基本面脱节的巨大泡沫中，泡沫迟早会破裂。
• **技术工具的扩展需求**：[kubb] 提出应为CLI工具（如Claude Code）开发LSP扩展，以便在编辑器中展示差异和完成代码，这将极大提升工具价值，并批评科技公司资金过剩但提供的实际价值有限。
• **交易透明性与误解**：[_jab] 认为公众在信息不完整的情况下对交易做出了误判，并赞扬相关公司保密工作到位，同时暗示公众可能永远不会了解全部细节，批评此前的一些误导性言论。
• **收购的价值与合理性**：[cheriot] 对Google花费20亿美元进行收购表示质疑，认为需要巨大的市场回报才能使这笔交易显得合理，但也认为存在可能性。
• **交易细节的模糊性**：[akavi] 对Windsurf的收购细节表示困惑，质疑是否存在普通股东未得到补偿的情况。
• **AI工具的实际能力**：[prakashn27] 认为当前的AI编码工具（如LLM）在实际应用中仍无法替代人类，特别是在复杂场景下，表明距离通用人工智能（AGI）还很远。
• **人才与公司结构的变化**：[oytis] 和 [krat0sprakhar] 对Google收购Windsurf后的人才分配和公司结构变化表示困惑和质疑，认为高级人才获得好处而普通工程师则面临整合。

补充讨论：
• **AI软件工程师的竞争与市场价值**：[rwyinuse] 质疑高估值AI软件工程师公司的市场竞争力和护城河，认为如果成功，任何人都可以利用其产品构建竞争产品，只是LLM的SaaS包装。
• **产品与品牌的整合**：[makin] 澄清了Cognition和Devin的关系，指出收购后产品和品牌的整合是合理的，但对收购金额表示惊讶。
• **技术差异与估值的合理性**：[isodev] 对Windsurf与其他AI公司（如OpenAI/Claude）之间的技术差异和估值合理性表示困惑。

争议焦点：
• 当前科技公司的高估值与实际市场价值和贡献是否匹配。
• 收购交易中的细节不透明导致的各种猜测和误解。
• AI技术在实际应用中的局限性与其高估值之间的矛盾。

Cognition’s acquisition of Windsurf
Cognition has signed a definitive agreement to acquire Windsurf, the agentic IDE.
2025-07-14
Scott Wu
In this post:
Follow us on:
Linkedin
Twitter | x
We’re excited to share that Cognition has signed a definitive agreement to acquire Windsurf, the agentic IDE.
The acquisition includes Windsurf’s IP, product, trademark and brand, and strong business. Above all, it includes Windsurf’s world-class people, some of the best talent in our industry, whom we’re privileged to welcome to our team.
In the immediate term, the Windsurf team will continue to operate as they have been, and we will remain focused on our work of accelerating your engineering with Devin. Over the coming months, we’ll be investing heavily in integrating Windsurf’s capabilities and unique IP into Cognition’s products.
With this deal, we’re doubling down on our mission of building the future of software engineering.
Below is the note I sent to the Cognition team this morning:
Team,
As discussed during our all-hands, we are acquiring Windsurf. We have now signed a definitive agreement and we couldn’t be more excited. Here’s a recap and, again, this information is highly confidential until 11am PT, after Windsurf’s all-hands. The Windsurf team deserves to hear this from Jeff and me in the right way, so please keep everything quiet in the interim out of respect for our new colleagues.
So, what exactly is the deal? With this acquisition, Cognition will own Windsurf’s beloved product and strong business:
The Windsurf IDE, now with
full
access to the latest Claude models
Windsurf's IP, including their trademark and the strong brand they have built
$82M of ARR and a fast-growing business, with enterprise ARR doubling quarter-over-quarter
A user base that includes 350+ enterprise customers and hundreds of thousands of daily active users
Above all, we are welcoming some of the most impressive people in our industry, including world-class GTM, engineering, and product teams.
We’ve long admired the Windsurf team and what they’ve built. One of my top priorities in structuring this deal was to honor their talent, hard work, and accomplishments in making Windsurf the great business it is today.
To that end, Jeff and I worked together to ensure that every single employee is treated with respect and well taken care of in this transaction. Specifically:
100% of Windsurf employees will participate financially in this deal
100% of Windsurf employees will have vesting cliffs waived for their work to date
100% of Windsurf employees will receive fully accelerated vesting for their work to date
Every new employee of Cognition will be treated the same way as existing employees: with transparency, fairness, and deep respect for their abilities and value. After today, our efforts will be as a united and aligned team. There’s only one boat and we’re all in it together.
What this means for Cognition is that we’ll be able to move even faster on our mission of building the future of software engineering. As you all know, we’ve had strong momentum and adoption over the last few months. For many enterprise engineering teams, Devin is already a top contributor. As our customer base continues to grow, it’s clear that combining the rapid adoption of Devin as the leading fully autonomous agent with Windsurf’s IDE product and scaled GTM machine will be a massive unlock.
There’s never been a more exciting time to build. Within our lifetime, engineers will go from bricklayers to architects, focusing on the creativity of designing systems rather than the manual labor of putting them together.
It’s a privilege to be in this position, and it’s your hard work that has brought us here. There’s much more to do ahead, and the work won’t be easy, but today is a huge win for all of us in the positive-sum game we’re playing. Thank you for being on this journey together. Now let’s get ready to give our new colleagues a warm welcome.

data.title: Embedding user-defined indexes in Apache Parquet
data.author: jasim
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了如何在Apache Parquet文件中嵌入用户自定义索引，而无需更改文件格式或创建新格式。尽管Parquet文件通常只包含基本的Min/Max/Null Count统计信息和Bloom过滤器，但通过利用文件末尾的元数据和基于偏移量的地址，可以嵌入自定义索引结构，同时保持与其他Parquet读取器的兼容性。

文章以一个查询为例，说明了在处理跨多个文件的列值时，基本统计信息的不足。通过在文件末尾存储自定义索引（如列举文件中的所有国家值），可以显著提高查询性能。作者解释了Parquet文件的结构，包括标准索引（如Min/Max统计、页面索引和Bloom过滤器），并展示了如何使用Apache DataFusion读写自定义索引。

通过在Parquet文件中嵌入索引，可以避免外部索引的额外成本和同步风险，同时保持与标准Parquet读取器的兼容性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Parquet文件格式的扩展及其在新技术下的适应性

不同观点：
• Jasim认为这篇文章是为了回应一些新的文件格式倡议，尤其是针对Parquet文件格式逐渐显露出过时的批评。文章讨论了一种在不破坏向后兼容性的前提下扩展Parquet的方法，即通过在文件的脚注和数据页之间插入任意数据，这些数据可以被像DataFusion这样的查询引擎利用，而其他读者会忽略这些数据。这种方法通过嵌入索引来提升查询性能，例如加速特定值存在的判断，而无需扫描整个数据页。Jasim还认为这篇文章对列式数据存储提供了深入的探讨。

• Nelkins则关注该方法的通用性，提出这种技术是否能被标准化以便其他Parquet读者也能利用。Nelkins指出，当前方法似乎仅适用于DataFusion，若能推广到其他Parquet读者，将具有更广泛的应用价值。

补充讨论：
• Jasim强调了这种技术对查询性能的具体提升，比如在查询`WHERE nation = 'Singapore'`时，利用索引避免扫描整个数据集，即使已有min-max过滤器来优化扫描。
• Nelkins的问题引出了一个潜在的争议点，即该技术是否以及如何能够被更广泛地接受和应用，涉及Parquet格式的标准化问题。

通过这些观点，可以看出讨论的核心在于Parquet文件格式扩展的必要性、技术实现方法及其通用性。
